title: Research on AI Music Teaching Evaluation Model Based on Deep Learning
authors: J. Li; F. Yan
abstract: This paper designs and implements a deep neural network-based assessment framework, which efficiently analyzes students' learning data in multiple dimensions, including audio signals, performance accuracy, pitch, and rhythm. In this paper, we design and implement a deep neural network-based assessment framework, which efficiently analyzes students' learning data in multiple dimensions, including audio signal, performance accuracy, pitch and rhythm. Through a large number of experiments, the effectiveness of the model in the assessment of music teaching effectiveness is verified, and the results show that the model has high advantages in assessment accuracy, real-time and adaptability. Finally, this paper also explores the potential of the model in future AI music teaching and proposes directions for further optimization and promotion of its application. The study shows that the AI music teaching assessment model based on deep learning effectively promotes the innovative development of music education, and has important theoretical value and practical significance.

title: Adaptive Efficacy Assessment Method for Music Education via Multimodal Deep Learning Fusion
authors: W. Li
abstract: Addressing the limitations inherent in traditional music education assessment—specifically strong subjectivity, delayed feedback, and the loss of technical details due to single-modality information—this paper proposes a novel Adaptive Efficacy Assessment Method (MAAF) based on multimodal deep learning fusion. The method constructs an audio-visual dual-stream neural network architecture: the auditory channel utilizes an improved ResNet to extract high-dimensional acoustic features from Mel-spectrograms; the visual channel integrates OpenPose hand keypoint detection with Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Networks (ST-GCN) to capture fine-grained performance techniques, employing a confidence-based masking strategy to effectively suppress occlusion noise. Furthermore, to address the challenge of spatiotemporal asynchrony in heterogeneous data, we design a linear interpolation alignment strategy and an Adaptive Gated Attention Mechanism to realize dynamic weight allocation for audio-visual features. Empirical research based on the URMP dataset and a newly constructed Real-World Classroom Dataset (RWCD), validated by expert reliability tests, demonstrates that the proposed model achieves an assessment accuracy (PCC=0.898) that is significantly superior to mainstream SOTA architectures (e.g., Transformers). Furthermore, extensive experiments on heterogeneous instruments (e.g., Piano, Guitar) confirm the model's robustness and cross-domain generalization capabilities. The model effectively simulates the multi-sensory collaborative assessment logic of human experts.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Music Education: Trends, Challenges, and Future Directions
authors: C. A. N. Mazlan; S. I. Koning; M. Y. M. Yusoff; D. S. H. A. Hassim; R. Hidayatullah; S. Jamnongsarn
abstract: This study explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in music education through a bibliometric analysis and scoping review. It identifies key research trends, influential works, and emerging themes related to AI-driven pedagogical applications. Beyond mapping scholarly output, the study synthesizes findings to highlight how AI enhances music learning through personalized feedback, operational efficiency, and improved music literacy. The analysis offers insights into AI's role in curriculum design and instructional strategies and proposes actionable implications for educators and researchers. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of AI's impact and provide practical directions for advancing music education.

title: Design and Development of Automatic Arrangement System for Interactive Music Education Based on Deep Neural Network
authors: P. Chen
abstract: With the continuous development of deep learning technology and the increasing demand of music education, the automatic arrangement system of interactive music education has become a hot spot in research and practice. Aiming at this problem, this paper puts forward a design and development method of automatic arrangement system for interactive music education based on Deep Neural Network (DNN). Firstly, this paper introduces the overall architecture of the system, including the design of key modules such as music encoder, music generator and music decoder. Then, this article elaborates on the selection and design process of DNN models, using techniques such as self attention mechanism and Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to improve the system's modeling ability and generation effect on music sequences. This article conducted experiments using multiple music datasets to evaluate the quality, diversity, and user experience of the system's generated music works. The experimental results show that the system proposed in this paper performs well in the task of music generation, with good generation effect and user experience. On the whole, the automatic arrangement system of interactive music education based on DNN proposed in this paper provides new ideas and methods for the development of music education and music creation.

title: Design and Development of Music Intelligent Education System Based on Artificial Intelligence
authors: B. Xu
abstract: In traditional teaching, students may find it difficult to receive timely and personalized feedback, and some students may lose interest in music learning due to the monotony of traditional learning methods. This article aimed to design a music intelligent education system based on artificial intelligence (AI), providing rich learning content and personalized guidance to enhance students' interest in learning. The artificial intelligence based music intelligent education system designed in this article was divided into basic information management module, student music task management module, personalized recommendation module, interactive community module, and artificial intelligence algorithm module. It can monitor student performance, provide personalized feedback and guidance, help students improve, and provide a richer and more interesting learning experience. The experimental results of this article showed that under traditional music education, only 21 students were very interested in music, while under the music intelligent education system, there were 120 students who were very interested in music. The music intelligent education system based on artificial intelligence can not only compensate for the shortcomings of traditional music education, but also provide students with more personalized, efficient, and interesting learning experiences.

abstract: A robust representative dataset is a critical component in proper training of any neural network. title: SynthTab: Leveraging Synthesized Data for Guitar Tablature Transcription
authors: Y. Zang; Y. Zhong; F. Cwitkowitz; Z. Duan
abstract: Guitar tablature is a form of music notation widely used among guitarists. It captures not only the musical content of a piece, but also its implementation and ornamentation on the instrument. Guitar Tablature Transcription (GTT) is an important task with broad applications in music education, composition, and entertainment. Existing GTT datasets are quite limited in size and scope, rendering models trained on them prone to overfitting and incapable of generalizing to out-of-domain data. In order to address this issue, we present a methodology for synthesizing large-scale GTT audio using commercial acoustic and electric guitar plugins. We procure SynthTab, a dataset derived from DadaGP, which is a vast and diverse collection of richly annotated symbolic tablature. The proposed synthesis pipeline produces audio which faithfully adheres to the original fingerings and a subset of techniques specified in the tablature, and covers multiple guitars and styles for each track. Experiments show that pre-training a baseline GTT model on SynthTab can improve transcription performance when fine-tuning and testing on an individual dataset. More importantly, cross-dataset experiments show that pre-training significantly mitigates issues with overfitting.

title: Personalized Music Education: A Systematic Review of AI Generation Methods
authors: F. Carnovalini; L. Espírito Santo; G. A. Wiggins
abstract: Despite recent notable advances of AI-Education research, formal music education is still largely performed as it was at the beginning of the last century. Instrument technical practice especially is still largely performed in a classical setting with little use of modern technologies, possibly due to being a skill-based curriculum. While other researchers have argued for the potential benefits of using Artificial Intelligence for the personalization of music education, it still seems to be rare both in schools and in research. In this paper, we present a systematic literature review exploring the use of computational generation of exercises for personalized music learning, with a special interest in piano. To do so, we retrieve research papers that use AI to improve personalization in music education exploring both what computational methods can provide personalization in music teaching, and how frequently AI is actually used for generation in this context. We screened 360 papers retrieved from online repositories, selecting 40 relevant papers that would satisfy some minimal quality requirements. Analyzing the papers, we found that while there is interest from the scientific community in improving music education through AI and computational means more generally, AI is under-utilized for generation despite its potential for personalization. We found no examples of generation of piano technical exercises, and, more generally, that instrumental technique is indeed the aspect that has seen lesser use of AI enhancement, often limited to adding visualizations to normal instrumental practice.

title: TapToTab: Video-Based Guitar Tabs Generation Using AI and Audio Analysis
authors: A. Ghaleb; E. Elsadawy; I. Essam; S. -E. Zaky; M. Abdelhakim; N. Fahim; R. Bayoumi; H. Hindy
abstract: The automation of guitar tablature generation from video inputs holds significant promise for enhancing music education, transcription accuracy, and performance analysis. Existing methods face challenges with consistency and completeness, particularly in detecting fretboards and accurately identifying notes. To address these issues, this paper introduces an advanced approach leveraging deep learning, specifically YOLO models for real-time fretboard detection, and Fourier Transform-based audio analysis for precise note identification. Experimental results demonstrate substantial improvements in detection accuracy and robustness compared to traditional techniques. This paper outlines the development, implementation, and evaluation of these methodologies, aiming to revolutionize guitar instruction by automating the creation of guitar tabs from video recordings.

title: Harmonizing Engagement of An Innovative Framework for Inspiring Active Learning in Music Education
authors: H. M. Al-Jawahry; H. L. AI Sadi; E. A. Hussain; O. Muhsin; A. K. Tabaan
abstract: The topic of creative learning is a good starting point for thinking about techniques that improve students' experiences during instruction. Good teaching is like the tissue that connects student, instructor, and subject. The two most important aspects of teaching are teacher-student interactions and student participation. Discipline-based music education (DME) is the result of developing and implementing a comprehensive approach to art education in order to reach all students. As a result, disciplinary education in music incorporates private and public education, college and college music education, private and corporate philanthropy, professional development institutes, and government agencies to promote the broader concept of learning and teaching music, allowing all students greater access. Despite being recognized in many school commitment and music programs, the potential differences between the genres of music that support commitment have received little attention. This paper-based artificial intelligence for music education (AI-DME) evaluates vision, listening, touch, and thinking. The reasoning process uses big data to build the net of its neural network and generate algorithms, which it then applies to music perception, music cognition, music research, the creation of student-computer interaction, within the realm of professional music education, an innovative music perception, cognitive music, music creation, and all sorts of an innovative, interactive education system based on artificial intelligence technologies. The simulation results show a high accuracy ratio of 93.7%, efficiency ratio of 92.9%, performance ratio of 95.3%, precision ratio of 94.6%, recall rate of 90.5%, student engagement ratio of 91.8%, and mean square error rate of 20.8% when compared to other methods.

title: Guitar-TECHS: An Electric Guitar Dataset Covering Techniques, Musical Excerpts, Chords and Scales Using a Diverse Array of Hardware
authors: H. Pedroza; W. Abreu; R. M. Corey; I. R. Roman
abstract: Guitar-related machine listening research involves tasks like timbre transfer, performance generation, and automatic transcription. However, small datasets often limit model robustness due to insufficient acoustic diversity and musical content. To address these issues, we introduce Guitar-TECHS, a comprehensive dataset featuring a variety of guitar techniques, musical excerpts, chords, and scales. These elements are performed by diverse musicians across various recording settings. Guitar-TECHS incorporates recordings from two stereo microphones: an egocentric microphone positioned on the performer’s head and an exocentric microphone placed in front of the performer. It also includes direct input recordings and microphoned amplifier outputs, offering a wide spectrum of audio inputs and recording qualities. All signals and MIDI labels are properly synchronized. Its multi-perspective and multi-modal content makes Guitar-TECHS a valuable resource for advancing data-driven guitar research, and to develop robust guitar listening algorithms. We provide empirical data to demonstrate the dataset’s effectiveness in training robust models for Guitar Tablature Transcription.

title: Research on Action Recognition and Feedback System in Piano Teaching Based on Deep Learning
authors: T. Xu
abstract: This article mainly explores the intelligent path of piano education technology, and develops a piano action recognition and feedback system based on DL (Deep learning) to improve the efficiency and quality of piano teaching. In order to achieve this goal, this article adopts the method of combining CNN (Convolutional neural network) and RNN (Recurrent neural network), and constructs an algorithm model of piano action recognition. By extensively collecting and preprocessing the video data of piano performance, the model is trained to accurately identify the gestures and action sequences of the players. In the experimental verification stage, several groups of control experiments are designed to compare the performance of the new algorithm with the existing technology in recognition accuracy, processing speed and user satisfaction. The results show that the new algorithm has achieved remarkable advantages in all assessment indexes. In the recognition of complex performance movements, the accuracy of the new algorithm is improved by nearly 20%, and the processing speed is also greatly improved, realizing real-time feedback. The user satisfaction survey further confirmed the effectiveness of the new system, and students generally indicated that the feedback provided by the system was more accurate and useful. This study provides a strong support for the intelligent transformation of piano education.

title: The Usage of Artificial Intelligence Technology in Music Education System Under Deep Learning
authors: Y. Chen; Y. Sun
abstract: This work addresses the needs of the music generation field by developing a music generation system based on an advanced Transformer model. The system incorporates an adaptive music feature encoder and a music emotion-driven multi-task learning framework. By integrating music theory knowledge and dynamic weight adjustment, the adaptive encoder can accurately capture different music styles and emotional characteristics. The multi-task learning framework enhances the model’s ability to generate music with emotional depth by using emotion tags. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves significant performance improvements on the Lakh MIDI Dataset (LMD). This is specifically reflected in scores that are above the industry average: a Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score of 0.43, a Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE-L) score of 0.63, and a Metric for Evaluation of Translation with Explicit ORdering (METEOR) score of 0.31. Additionally, teaching methods based on music generation models have shown significant advantages in enhancing students’ musical skills, emotional expression abilities, and overall satisfaction. These results not only demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method but also highlight its potential applications in music education and automated music composition.

title: Innovation and Application of Virtual Reality Technology in the Integration Path of Music Education Industry and Education in Local Universities
authors: L. Ailing
abstract: In exploring new ways of integrating music education industry and education in local universities, virtual reality (VR) technology, as a cutting-edge technology, is gradually demonstrating its enormous potential and importance. With the fully immersive experience and high interactivity of VR technology, it has created a new learning environment for music education, greatly enriching teaching methods and profoundly transforming students' learning methods from traditional passive acceptance to active exploration and practice. This article provides a detailed analysis of the application strategies and innovative practices of VR technology in the integration of music education in local universities, and proposes a feedback and intelligent evaluation system that combines VR technology with deep learning (DL) algorithms. This system can simulate real music performance scenes, allowing students to experience near real performance or singing in a virtual environment, and quickly analyze students' performance using DL algorithms to provide personalized feedback and guidance, thereby significantly improving the accuracy and efficiency of teaching. Experimental results have shown that this system not only greatly stimulates students' interest and participation in learning, but also effectively promotes the rapid improvement of students' music skills.

title: Design and Application of Music Cloud Teaching Platform based on Artificial Intelligence Algorithm
authors: L. Xue
abstract: The rapid evolution of intelligent education platforms has greatly transformed traditional teaching methodologies, especially in music education. However, existing digital platforms do not offer adaptive, efficient, and context-sensitive learning experiences. To address these limitations, this research develops an adaptive cloud-based music education system powered by a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) algorithm. By modeling the sequential and temporal dependencies of musical elements, the proposed system supports real-time analysis of learner interaction patterns and enhances intelligent content delivery. The dataset used in this study comprises a diverse collection of user interaction data, audio features, and performance evaluations gathered from an online music learning environment. The BiLSTM model was employed to predict user skill levels and generate personalized learning paths. Experimental results demonstrated an accuracy of 98.2%, outperforming other learning models and confirming its effectiveness in addressing individual learner needs. title: A Real-Time Adaptive Music Performance Assistance and Training System using Attentionbased CNN-BiLSTM with Genetic Optimization
authors: J. Yu
abstract: In modern times, music learning progressively transformed towards intelligent digital platforms which guide learners in enhancing their music performance using automated analysis and feedback. However, existing Attention-Induced Multi-Head Convolutional Neural Network Optimized with Hunter-Prey Optimization (AIMCNN-HPO) lacks in real-time feedback ability, unable to capture temporal dependencies, depends on computationally heavy HPO and gives no personalized learning adaptation. To address these limitations, Adaptive Learning Attention-Based Convolutional Neural Network-Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory system Optimized with Genetic Algorithm (ACNN-BiLSTM-GA) is proposed. Primarily, audio data collected from Piano Triads Wavset dataset and preprocessed using Adaptive Distorted Gaussian Matched Filter (ADGMF) and normalization to ensure standardize input for model training. Next, feature extraction is employed utilizing Mel-spectrograms, MelFrequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs). Further, these features fed to CNN-Attention-BiLSTM network which allows both spatial learning and temporal modeling. Furthermore, GA used for effectively tuning hyperparameters and decrease computational load. Additionally, real-time analysis allows instant feedback and personalized learning component adaptively adjusts difficultly and practice suggestions based on history. Together, these components convert framework into adaptive, interactive music training assistant. Therefore, proposed ACNN-BiLSTM-GA achieved greater results in accuracy ($\mathbf{4 5 \%}$), Learning Skill Ratio (99%), Learning Activity Ratio (99%), Student Performance Rate (99.2%), Teaching Evaluation Rate (95%) And Learning Behavior Rate (99.5%).

title: Intrusion Detection System To Secure AI-powered E-Learning Platforms Against Various Cyberattacks
authors: A. Ayoubi; L. Laaouina; A. Jeghal; H. Tairi
abstract: AI-powered E-learning represents a major step forward toward more effective and flexible education. Despite the challenges it poses, the opportunities it offers make it an essential choice for improving the educational process in the future. The integration of AI is mainly achieved through E-learning platforms, which are the key technological support. When powered by AI, these platforms become not only learning spaces, but also intelligent environments. However, this technological evolution introduces new vulnerabilities and attack surfaces. Cyberattacks via advanced attacks exploit these flaws to compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and reliability of the system, affecting the effectiveness and credibility of these platforms. It is therefore essential to identify these emerging risks and implement intelligent security mechanisms to protect digital learning platforms. This also requires constant attention and well-defined security measures to ensure an educational environment that is not only innovative but also safe, reliable, and secure.This article examines the main cyber risks faced by online learning platforms that integrate artificial intelligence. It highlights the value of integrating intrusion detection systems (IDS) based on deep learning techniques, particularly for identifying both traditional attacks and those specifically related to the use of AI in smart educational environments. The article also proposes a suitable architecture for this system, accompanied by countermeasures designed to enhance the security of AI-powered E-learning platforms.

title: Design and Development of University Vocal Music Teaching System Based on Optimized Neural Network
authors: L. Liang
abstract: With the increasing integration of artificial intelligence into art and music education, the demand for intelligent and adaptive vocal training systems is growing. This study presents the design and development of a university-level vocal music teaching system powered by an optimized neural network model, aiming to enhance vocal instruction through personalized feedback, real-time analysis, and data-driven progress tracking. The proposed system employs a hybrid neural architecture combining Bidirectional LSTM (Bi-LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), optimized using Bayesian hyper parameter tuning to improve pitch detection, tone quality analysis, and vocal range classification. The system also features a voiceprint database, real-time spectrogram visualization, and AI-assisted scoring mechanisms for vocal exercises. A dataset of over 1 2, 0 0 0 annotated vocal samples from classical, pop, and ethnic music performances was used to train the model. Experimental results demonstrated a pitch recognition accuracy of 99.3 %, with a mean squared error of 0.008 in tone deviation detection. In practical classroom deployment with 150 music students, the system led to a 30 % improvement in vocal training efficiency, as measured by instructor assessments and student feedback. This intelligent vocal music teaching platform enables adaptive learning, objective evaluation, and enhanced vocal training, offering a novel and effective approach to modernizing music education in higher institutions

title: An Intelligent Assessment System for Yao Suona Performance Techniques Based on a Cross-Spectral Temporal Adaptive Attention Model

abstract: Traditional folk instrument assessments suffer from low efficiency, poor consistency, and lack of visual feedback. Moreover, the accompanying visualization module presents performance differences in pitch, rhythm, and technique. It uses multiscale heatmaps and pitch deviation charts. The module supports segment analysis and interactive zooming. This aids targeted improvements. The system integrates audio input, feature extraction, temporal modeling, prediction, and visualization output. It forms a complete closed loop. Experiments show the framework outperforms traditional methods in accuracy, speed, and user experience. User surveys also indicate strong practicality and instructional value. However, the study also notes room for improvement in data diversity, streaming feedback, and model extension. Future work will explore additional instrument types. We will adopt advanced architectures and integrate with online teaching platforms.

title: Separate and Transcribe: Deep Guitar String Separation and its Application for Tablature Transcription Enhancement
authors: G. Bastas; V. Katsouros; P. Maragos
abstract: Guitar string separation constitutes a source separation task in which the individual stems to be retrieved are the signals produced by each distinct guitar string. Certain hardware solutions for string-wise signal manipulation are gaining traction among the guitarist community for applications such as MIDI control and string-level sound effects. However, software techniques for string separation are lagging behind, even though they could form a competitive alternative. This work applies established deep learning architectures commonly used for standard music source separation, to address the task of guitar string separation. It opts for a waveform-to-waveform approach using a multi-channel version of Wave-U-Net. It further suggests that this model can serve as a bridge from separation to transcription by facilitating guitar tablature inference. Tablature transcription enhancement proved feasible using a method that relies on feeding the separated signals to standard tablature inference models, by simply modifying their initial convolution layer to handle multi-source input. Moreover, this work seeks to address the challenges encountered in the more specific string separation scenario where no target signals are readily available for training, meaning that these signals are not provided directly through sophisticated hardware equipment such as polyphonic pickups. Instead, data manipulation and augmentation techniques that produce sample-level synthesized targets are proposed. Thus, two newly created datasets are introduced, namely GS-Aux and ADGP, based on standard guitar datasets: GuitarSet and DadaGP.

title: Temporal Modeling of Classical Piano Music using GRU-based Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: L. Simhadri; K. Venkatesh; R. Uyyala; P. Vurubindi
abstract: This Paper introduces a recurrent neural network framework for music generation focusing on modeling the timing of notes in classical piano music. The system utilizes stacked recurrent neural networks with gated recurrent units (GRU), trained on Maestro dataset, which includes over 200 hours of aligned MIDI and audio recordings-from global piano compositions. Distinct from traditional methods involving generative adversarial networks or transformer models, our approach highlights how deep temporal modeling of note-onset sequences enables the generation of coherent, long-form compositions while maintaining stylistic fidelity. The proposed model attains a note prediction accuracy of 89.6 percent on the validation set by employing curriculum learning strategies that incrementally address polyphonic complexity. Quantitative assessment based on the Music Theory Similarity Index (MTSI) demonstrates an 82.4 percent alignment with classical harmonic progressions, outperforming baseline LSTM models by 14.2 percent. The primary contribution lies in the introduction of a dynamic temperature sampling mechanism, which effectively balances exploration and exploitation during generation, thereby mitigating the over-smoothing phenomenon commonly observed in recurrent neural network-based systems. This study advances automated composition systems by illustrating that targeted temporal modeling of single-instrument repertoires can achieve higher stylistic fidelity than generalized multi-instrument frame-works. The findings indicate strong potential for applications in computer-assisted composition and music education, particularly in preserving historical performance practices through AI-based analysis and generation. This work addresses these challenges by leveraging Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs), a variant of recurrent neural networks known for their efficiency and effectiveness in modeling sequential data with long-term dependencies.

title: Real-Time Feedback Application for Musical Pitch Training in Deaf Individuals Using Knowledge of Results
authors: J. Hyun Yi; M. Hwang; P. Mane
abstract: People who are deaf have difficulty singing due to pitch recognition issues, even when using hearing aids or cochlear implants. This study addresses this issue by developing an interactive training application that provides real-time visual feedback, including Knowledge of Results (KR)—external feedback indicating whether the sung pitch matches the intended note. When a user produces a sound, the application detects its pitch using RAPT (Robust Algorithm for Pitch Tracking) and displays the corresponding musical note. A real-time pitch slider allows users to monitor and adjust their pitch relative to the target note. This dual-feedback mechanism enables users to actively regulate their vocal output during practice. The system was tested in four singing training sessions with ten participants who are deaf. As a result, the participants were able to successfully sing “Twinkle Twinkle Little Star.” The training enabled them to improve pitch and volume control and to develop a foundational understanding of basic singing techniques. This application demonstrates the potential to provide effective singing training for people who are deaf who have traditionally been excluded from music education. By supporting self-regulated learning through visual and interactive feedback, the system offers a meaningful educational tool to promote inclusivity in music learning for the deaf community.

title: Adaptive Segmentation of EEG for Machine Learning Applications
authors: J. Zhou; J. West; K. A. Ehinger; Z. Ren; S. E. John; D. B. Grayden
abstract: Objective. Electroencephalography (EEG) data is derived by sampling continuous neurological time series signals. In order to prepare EEG signals for machine learning, the signal must be divided into manageable segments. The current naive approach uses arbitrary fixed time slices, which may have limited biological relevance because brain states are not confined to fixed intervals. We investigate whether adaptive segmentation methods are beneficial for machine learning EEG analysis. Approach. We introduce a novel adaptive segmentation method, CTXSEG, that creates variable-length segments based on statistical differences in the EEG data and propose ways to use them with modern machine learning approaches that typically require fixed-length input. We assess CTXSEG using controllable synthetic data generated by our novel signal generator CTXGEN. We validate on a real-world use case by replacing fixed-length segmentation in the preprocessing step of a typical EEG machine learning pipeline for seizure detection, and offer guidance on how application may be extended to other problem domains. Main results. We found that using CTXSEG to prepare EEG data improves seizure detection performance compared to fixed-length approaches when evaluated using a standardized framework, without modifying the machine learning method, and requires fewer segments. Significance. This work demonstrates that adaptive segmentation with CTXSEG can be readily applied to modern machine learning approaches, with potential to improve performance. It is a promising alternative to fixed-length segmentation for signal preprocessing and should be considered as part of the standard preprocessing repertoire in EEG machine learning applications.

title: Research on Music Course Teaching Resource Recommendation based on Convolutional Neural Network
authors: Y. Gu
abstract: The fast development of online education calls for smart recommendation systems that can improve personalized music learning experiences. This paper introduces a Hierarchical Multi-Modal Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based recommendation model that can be specifically designed for the teaching resources of music courses. Current recommendation systems are plagued by low accuracy, poor contextual understanding, and limited adaptability to the distinctive auditory and structural properties of music-oriented data. Classic models like collaborative filtering and content-based ones tend to be ineffective in representing profound semantic relations between musical resources. However, the proposed architecture digs out hierarchical features from multi-modal music data (textual, audio, and visual inputs) to predict learner preferences accurately and provide relevant recommendations. The model's resilience and flexibility attest to its applicability in practical situations in dynamic learning environments, providing an intelligent and effective means for resource recommendation in music learning.

title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Evaluation System of Traditional Chinese Music Performance
authors: S. Peng
abstract: Ancient Chinese music, with its rich cultural meanings and expressive subtleties, is quite challenging to objectively evaluate because it is interpretative, sensitive to tones, and heterogeneous in terms of style. Current systems of evaluation depend on the expert's subjective feedback or predetermined rubric scores, which are typically associated with inconsistencies, low scalability, and non-tailored treatment. To address these challenges, this research introduces an innovative intelligent assessment system that combined hybrid model to evaluate musical performances accurately and with stylistic sensitivity. The system receives audio inputs through sophisticated signal processing methods, extracting the most important musical features like pitch accuracy, rhythm stability, timbre tone, and dynamic intensity. These characteristics are subsequently examined by the deep learning model that has been trained on expert-annotated traditional Chinese music performances, mimicking human-like assessment patterns. Experimental confirmation on the dataset compiled for varied musical content yields excellent results with an accuracy of 96.6%, precision of 96.6%, recall of 96.4%, and an F1-score of 96.5%. This smart system not only increases consistency and interpretability but also provides useful real-time feedback for students and teachers, making it a potential tool for furthering the contemporary pedagogy of Chinese traditional music education.

title: Real-time Guitar Chord Recognition Using Keypoint Detection and Neural Network-Based Inter-Keypoint Distance Classifier
authors: M. R. Rasyid; M. D. Sulistiyo; F. Sthevanie; G. S. Wulandari; D. Haryadi
abstract: This research addresses the significant challenge of real-time guitar chord recognition, focusing on improving accuracy in finger placement for chord playing. Real-time guitar chord recognition poses a significant challenge, particularly in accurately detecting and classifying chords during dynamic playing sessions. Existing methods often struggle with variations in finger placement, chord shapes, and orientations, leading to lower accuracy and usability in practical scenarios. This research aims to develop a robust and efficient chord recognition model capable of operating seamlessly in real-time, enhancing the overall guitar playing experience for musicians. The proposed solution combines keypoint detection and a neural network-based model, with the usage of inter-keypoint distances achieving an impressive 88.24% accuracy for a 7-chord classifier in testing. Google's Mediapipe framework for keypoint detection is utilized to address the complexities of real-time chord recognition. The study evaluates the model's performance in handling non-horizontal guitar orientations and distinguishing chords with similar shapes, demonstrating significant advancements in real-time chord recognition accuracy and usability. By addressing the complexities of real-time chord recognition, this research contributes to enhancing the usability and accuracy of chord recognition systems in practical guitar playing scenarios, benefiting musicians and music enthusiasts alike. Further exploration and refinement of this approach are recommended for continued improvement in real-time guitar chord recognition technology.

This article will describe how to build an intelligent machine, consisting of both hardware and software, that can replicate and exceed the abilities of the human brain in order to handle complicated issues that need specialized knowledge. It will specifically examine how to more effectively use artificial intelligence support systems into piano instruction. An Introduction, an oral language and music-assisted education system based on the ARM and SA algorithm, is proposed by this study in order to ascertain the implementation principle guiding the functioning of the piano automation recording system. It also delves deeply into the theory and operation of automated music recording systems, compiling and evaluating data that these systems generate via internal databases. is an effort to improve music education via the use of artificial intelligence support systems. title: Bibliometric Analysis of Research Topics and Mining Characteristics in “AI in Education”
authors: C. Liu; Y. Zhu
abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence(AI) technology, the deep integration and organic combination of AI with traditional pedagogy has emerged as one of the most prominent research themes in educational technology. It has also garnered significant attention from governments, enterprises, research institutions, and educators worldwide. To investigate the research hotspots and developmental trends in AI in Education, this study analyzes literature from the Web of Science database spanning 2010 to 2025 in this field. Leveraging methodologies from scientific knowledge mapping and visualization analysis via CiteSpace software, we systematically map the research landscape of AI in Education through multiple dimensions: temporal distribution of publications, keyword co-occurrence and clustering analyses, timeline and burst detection analyses. This work aims to synthesize existing research achievements, identify critical issues and future directions worthy of scholarly attention, and provide actionable insights to guide subsequent research and development in this domain.

title: Deep Learning-Driven Recommendation Framework for Personalized College Vocal Music Education
authors: Y. Fang
abstract: In recent years, Vocal music recommendation systems have developed crucial components of digital learning platforms that supports the personalized content delivery in educational settings. However, traditional models significantly depend on user listening history often fail to deliver accurate recommendations for new users leads to cold-start limitations. Hence, this research proposes an enhanced hybrid recommendation framework that incorporates the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with Variational Autoencoder (VAE) to overcome these challenges. Initially, user behavioral data were gathered from public music datasets in the form of play counts and audio content. Then, the behavioral data were normalized and converted into a user–music interaction matrix, while audio signals were preprocessed into Log-Mel spectrograms. After that, the processed data were fed into CNN model to extract high-level acoustic features from the spectrograms for creating the compact content embeddings for each song. Further, a VAE-based preference modeling approach was employed to learn latent user distributions and make initial preference vectors for new users without interaction history. Finally, the proposed CNN–VAE framework produced top-n recommendations by matching audio content features with created user embeddings. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed CNN–VAE framework attained greater performance in terms of accuracy of 0.94% compared to existing CNN model.

title: Exploring the Use of Virtual Reality and AI to Create Immersive, Interactive Music Experiences for Performance, Education, and Therapy
authors: J. Zhao; K. Cheng
abstract: This study investigates the synchronization of real-time music generation with visual elements in Virtual Reality (VR) environments, leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) to create immersive, interactive music experiences for performance, education, and therapy. By leveraging deep learning techniques, specifically Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, the study investigates real-time music generation and synchronization with VR environments. The optimization of music-visual alignment was achieved through Genetic Algorithms (GAs), enhancing the overall coherence and responsiveness of the system. Key findings include significant improvements in user engagement, learning outcomes, and audience satisfaction in educational and performance contexts. The system achieved a high degree of musical coherence, with sequence prediction accuracy of 92.3% and sub-50ms latency, providing a seamless VR music experience. Case studies focused on interactive music education, immersive performance, and personalized music therapy demonstrated the system’s potential in diverse settings, with improvements in user retention, stress reduction, and overall satisfaction. This study highlights the transformative potential of combining VR and AI in music, paving the way for innovative applications in music education, performance, and therapy. The findings offer a foundation for future research and development in immersive music technologies.

title: Personalized Remote Piano Education via an AI-Empowered Teacher–Student Framework
authors: M. Han; G. Y. Li
abstract: After COVID-19, remote education has emerged as new pedagogical paradigm. However, traditional teacher-to-many-students instructional systems remain ill-equipped to deliver personalized guidance and granular feedback, thus online teaching quality needs to be enhanced urgently. To overcome this limitation, we propose an AIpowered personalized remote education framework that leverages artificial intelligence’s generalization capabilities and adaptability to achieve large-scale personalized instruction. Within our proposed twostage teacher-AI-student paradigm, the teacher first instructs a general AI agent, which is subsequently specialized to tutor individual students. We validate this framework through a personalized remote piano instruction case: A Transformer-based music transcription model converts performance audio into symbolic MIDI sequences, while the teacherinstructed AI agent refines these sequences into expressive performance versions. The resulting teacherstudent performance comparison data provides students with personalized feedback on note onset timing and dynamics. To assess the effectiveness of the proposed framework, we collected piano proficiency examination data encompassing approximately 30 distinct pieces by different composers. Each piece’s performance is treated as an independent student, thereby allowing us to analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed framework in providing personalized feedback to students. Experimental results across multiple piano pieces demonstrate that this framework effectively captures performance variations, delivers explainable feedback, and balances efficiency with personalized needs in remote learning environments.

title: Automatic Guitar Transcription With Deep Neural Networks
authors: S. Chieppa; P. Brutti; R. Pedro Paiva
abstract: Guitar tablature is a form of musical notation designed specifically for fretted string instruments. It is crucial for musicians, especially beginners, as it provides an easy-to-read format that visually represents the placement of the fingers on the instrument, making it more accessible to learn and play songs accurately. Automatic transcription of guitar music into tablature is a complex task in Music Information Retrieval, which has been enhanced by recent advances in deep learning. This article builds on a state-of-the-art note-level transcription model that uses a self-attention mechanism. The model incorporates beat-informed quantisation to accurately convert audio signals into tablature, overcoming challenges such as determining where notes are played on the guitar neck. In replicating this model, its properties have been investigated, and the results have been analysed. A key aspect of this article is the development of a new dataset designed to assess the robustness of the model in different scenarios. This is crucial due to the limited availability of data in this area. Through extensive experimentation and analysis, this study evaluates the performance of the model on unseen data, identifying its strengths and areas for improvement. In addition, this article provides insights into the mechanism of self-attention and its effectiveness in tasks such as Automatic Music Transcription. The model was tested with multiple attention heads to study their impact on performance, but this modification did not show significant improvement. Therefore, it suggests that other areas, such as improving the quality and quantity of data, may be more crucial to improve performance.

title: A Human-Centered Learning and Teaching Framework Using Generative Artificial Intelligence for Self-Regulated Learning Development Through Domain Knowledge Learning in K–12 Settings
authors: S. -C. Kong; Y. Yang
abstract: The advent of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has ignited an increase in discussions about generative AI tools in education. In this study, a human-centered learning and teaching framework that uses generative AI tools for self-regulated learning development through domain knowledge learning was proposed to catalyze changes in educational practices. The framework illustrates how generative AI tools can revolutionize educational practices and transform the processes of teaching and learning to become human-centered. It emphasizes the evolving roles of teachers, who increasingly become skillful facilitators and humanistic storytellers who craft differentiated instructions and attempt to develop students’ individualized learning. Drawing upon insights from neuroscience, the framework guides students to employ generative AI tools to augment their attentiveness, stimulate active engagement in learning, receive immediate feedback, and encourage self-reflection. The pedagogical approach is also reimagined; teachers equipped with generative AI tools and AI literacy can refine their teaching strategies to better equip students to meet future challenges. The practical application of the framework is demonstrated in a case study involving the development of Chinese language writing ability among primary students within a K–12 educational context. This article also reports the results of a 60-h development programme for teachers. Specifically, providing in-service teachers with cases involving uses of the proposed framework helped them to better understand the generative AI concepts and integrate them into their teaching and learning and increased their perceived ability to design AI-integrated courses that would enhance students’ attention, engagement, confidence, and satisfaction.

title: SmartPosture: Real-Time Violin Posture Evaluation and Feedback Using Pose Estimation and Haptic Correction
authors: A. Arora
abstract: This paper presents SmartPosture, a novel framework to evaluate violin posture accuracy by using computer vision and sensor-based feedback. An integrated solution was developed to evaluate real-time upper-body violin playing posture by combining Mediapipe's landmark posture coordinates with a custom Artificial Intelligence model to classify whether the posture was correct. In turn, this assessment system provides instant corrective feedback using an Arduino-based wearable haptic device. Through the evaluation process of testing different posture conditions while capturing real-time data, the model was able to classify common types of posture mistakes, such as shoulders sagging or incorrect wrist angles. The combination of computer vision, embedded systems, and machine learning model provides an agile and cost-effective posture correction system that supports remote and self-directed violin training for learners.

title: Exploring Machine Learning Algorithms for Accurate Indian Raaga Classification
authors: G. V. Soumya; G. C. Somashekhar; G. Preethi; B. D. Parameshachari; R. Paramesha; K. Puttegowda
abstract: Selective Raaga recognition has become an important task in recent years which can be used to identify the melodic modes of the Indian classical violin called GATs selectively from a given set of raagas. Thus, in this paper, we provide a detailed review on machine learning algorithms used for raaga recognition. We start by discussing the difficulties in raaga identification and analysis, including the intricate and difficult to model musical construction of raaga and subjectivity of raaga rendition. In the following sections that outline several methodologies of machine learning are used in raaga recognition: Hidden Markov Models (HMMs), Support Vector Machines (SVMs), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). For each of the algorithms, their applicability, weaknesses and strengths in the context of raaga recognition are discussed as follows. Furthermore, we shed light on the emergent studies, and future research directions within the scope of the domain. Concerning this evaluation is our hope to provide researchers and practitioners with a broad and profound understanding of present-day machine learning approaches for raaga recognition with the view to catalyze their advancement in the crucial sub-domain of MIR.

title: Research on the Application of Transformer, GAN and Q-learning in Piano Improvisational Accompaniment Teaching
authors: J. Wang
abstract: In recent years, the integration of cloud computing and artificial intelligence technologies has brought revolutionary changes to the field of education. This study proposes a cloud-based AI framework, leveraging Transformer, Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), and Q-learning technologies, aiming to optimize the efficiency and personalized experience of piano improvisational accompaniment teaching. Through Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), the digital conversion of audio signals into MIDI format is achieved, and digital information processing technology is used for feature extraction. The methods include system architecture design supported by distributed cloud computing, sequence modeling with Transformer, stylized accompaniment generation with GAN, and reinforcement learning optimization with Q-learning. Experiments were conducted using Muqam-style musical score data for testing, verifying the framework's adaptability under different emotional styles. The experimental results indicate that the framework significantly outperforms traditional teaching methods in terms of feedback accuracy (96.1%±1.2%), learning efficiency (improved by 34.7%±3.5%), model stability (variance 0.015), and response time (0.22 seconds). This research provides a new paradigm for the engineering application of AI technology in the field of music education. Future work may further optimize performance in high-concurrency scenarios.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Music Curriculum Design
authors: J. Jin
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive curriculum generation model designed to enable personalized course delivery and optimize real-time teaching feedback mechanisms. The results show that the model has significant benefits in improving learning outcomes, maintaining interest, and facilitating skills transfer.

title: Intelligent and Objective Assessment of Music Teaching Quality based on Neural Network Framework
authors: M. Lin; J. Jiao
abstract: The assessment of music teaching quality is very challenging because it involves subjective evaluation approaches, varied teaching styles, and unique student responses to learning. Conventional assessment methods mainly depend on student responses and manual grading, which are usually biased and inconsistent. Current automated systems apply statistical models and rule-based methods but fail to catch the intricate relationship between the effectiveness of teaching and student activities in music learning. To overcome these limitations, this research introduces a sophisticated neural network-based approach that efficiently evaluates several indicators of teaching quality, such as the clarity of lectures, student participation, musical skill acquisition, and patterns of understanding. The suggested model greatly enhances evaluation accuracy and reduces subjective biases, yielding a more objective and integrated assessment. Experimental results on real-world educational data show that the proposed model attains a 97% accuracy, surpassing traditional models in reliability and efficacy. By providing a scalable and solid solution, this framework enhances the development of intelligent music teaching evaluation systems.

title: Design and Application of Experiential Music Teaching System based on Java 2 Enterprise Edition Architecture
authors: L. Huang; Y. Zheng
abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and web-based technologies, music education has evolved beyond conventional teaching methodologies, offering more interactive and adaptive learning experiences. This paper presents the design and application of an Experiential Music Teaching System based on J2EE (Java 2 Enterprise Edition) architecture, integrating AI-driven techniques to enhance personalized learning, automatic assessment, and real-time feedback. The system is structured using a three-tier architecture, consisting of a presentation layer (UI), business logic layer (middleware), and data layer (database), ensuring scalability, flexibility, and seamless user interaction. To deliver personalized learning experiences, AI algorithms Reinforcement Learning (RL) are leveraged to recommend music lessons tailored to an individual's progress, learning style, and skill level. The AI models analyse user performance data, adjusting lesson plans dynamically to optimize the learning curve. Additionally, deep learning techniques enable automatic assessment of instrumental and vocal performances, analyzing audio features such as pitch, rhythm, and tone for accurate evaluation. The J2EE-based system ensures seamless integration of AI models through RESTful APIs, allowing real-time data exchange between the front-end and back-end services. This architecture facilitates an efficient and responsive environment where students can practice, receive instant feedback, and track their progress over time. By merging AI-powered analytics with modern music pedagogy, the system bridges the gap between traditional music instruction and digital learning environments, offering students an interactive, self-paced, and feedback-driven approach to mastering musical skills. Future enhancements may incorporate gesture recognition for instrument training, AI-assisted composition tools, and adaptive tutoring strategies to further refine the learning process.

title: Optimization of Intelligent Recommendation Algorithms and System Design for Online Music Education
authors: H. Xu; F. Yan
abstract: With the vigorous development of online education, the field of music education has also ushered in a wave of digital transformation. However, how to accurately recommend content that meets users' individual needs in massive music courses has become an urgent problem. Based on this, this article designs and implements a hybrid recommendation strategy. This strategy combines content-based music course recommendation and collaborative filtering-based learning partner recommendation. It aims to provide users with more comprehensive and accurate recommendation services. In this article, a data set containing rich user behavior data and course information is constructed, and the quality and consistency of the data are ensured through data cleaning and preprocessing. By calculating the accuracy and other assessment indicators, and collecting user satisfaction feedback, the performance of the algorithm is comprehensively assessed. The assessment results show that the proposed hybrid recommendation strategy scores well in all assessment indexes, especially in accuracy and user satisfaction. This verifies the effectiveness of the hybrid recommendation strategy and shows its great potential in the field of online music education.

title: Using Hybrid Models for Action Correction in Instrument Learning Based on AI
authors: A. Enkhbat; T. K. Shih; M. Gochoo; P. Cheewaprakobkit; W. Aditya; T. Duy Quy; H. Lin; Y. -T. Lin
abstract: Human action recognition has recently attracted much attention in computer vision research. Its applications are widely found in video surveillance, human-computer interaction, entertainment, and autonomous driving. In this study, we developed a system for evaluating online music performances. This system conducts experiments to assess performance of playing the erhu, the most popular traditional stringed instrument in East Asia. Mastering the erhu poses a challenge, as players often struggle to enhance their skills due to incorrect techniques and a lack of guidance, resulting in limited progress. To address this issue, we propose hybrid models based on graph convolutional networks (GCN) and temporal convolutional networks (TCN) for action recognition to capture spatial relationships between different joints or keypoints in a human skeleton, and interactions between these joints. This can assist players in identifying errors while playing the instrument. In our research, we use RGB video as input, segmenting it into individual frames. For each frame, we extract keypoints, encompassing both image and keypoint information, which serve as input data for our model. Leveraging our innovative model architecture, we achieve an impressive accuracy rate exceeding 97% across various classes of hand error modules, thus providing valuable insights into the assessment of musical performances and demonstrates the potential of AI-based solutions to enhance the learning and correction of complex human actions in interactive learning environments.

title: Evaluating and Comparing Deep Learning Methods with Vision Transformers for Musical Key Assessment
authors: M. Divya; K. B. Anusha; D. V. Reddy; M. J. Shaik
abstract: A composition's major key is an essential component that helps with transposition and arrangement, providing information about the work's harmonic structure, tonal center, and chord progressions. Furthermore, precise key estimate finds use in both academic and industrial contexts, such as in computerized music recommendation systems and computerized music reproduction. By utilizing their successes in various domains, the current publication provides a thorough comparison between the conventional deep learning structures and the upcoming visualization converters. They estimate the outcomes by analyzing six distinct deep learning methods on a specific subset of gathered GTZAN dataset. Our findings show that Dense-Net, a traditional deep neural network architecture, outperforms visual transformers with an impressive 93.64 % accuracy; yet, we examine each deep learning method in more detail to clarify its temporal characteristics. In particular, the SWIN and vision transformers perform better in temporal metrics than the Dense-Net design, but they show a slight decrease in overall effectiveness (1.82 % and 2.39 %, respectively). Our results are noteworthy because they offer a practical instrument for musical key valuation, an area where precise and effective computational methods are essential. Through analyzing the advantages and disadvantages of image transformers and artificial neural networks, we might potentially obtain important data for real-world applications like automatic music transcription and product recommendation systems. Our research opens up new avenues for future advances and motivates further study in this field

title: Guitar Chord Recognition Using Sobel Feature Extraction and YOLOv8 Segmentation with CNN Classification
authors: M. A. S. Bin Syamsyul Syahar; Z. Zulkifli; I. A. Mohtar; M. Mohamad; S. Ahmad; M. I. M. Ariff
abstract: Music is created by blending musical sounds from various musical instruments. One of the famous musical instruments is the guitar. Learning to play the guitar is time-consuming and requires much patience, especially when starting. Picking up the basic theories and implementing them physically on the guitar, especially the basic seven chords, is hard at first and needs a lot of consistent practice. However, one needs a good grasp of the specific hand shape to play the basic chords, especially which finger to press on which string on the fretboard. This may lead some beginners to hit a plateau in their learning journey, causing them to give up on learning the guitar. To address the problem, this project proposes a web application prototype that utilises image processing techniques to aid beginners in detecting and classifying guitar chords from various visual media. The project aims to use image processing techniques to detect and classify guitar chords and implement them into a web application. To accomplish the objectives of this project, the YOLOv8 Segmentation method, which is utilised for assigning pixel-level labels to objects within an image, is employed, along with Sobel for feature extraction and a CNN functioning as the classifier. The chosen algorithm achieved an accuracy of 95 %. In conclusion, this prototype holds a promising potential as a valuable tool to aid new guitarists in their learning journey, specifically in detecting and classifying guitar chords. Future work may explore additional image processing techniques, such as shape descriptors and experiment with deeper CNN architectures to improve performance and generalisation across diverse visual inputs.

title: An Intelligent Music Teaching System Based on Lite Models and Android Platform
authors: S. Li
abstract: With the increasing demand for mobile and personalized education, the integration of music teaching with intelligent mobile platforms has become a crucial direction for innovation in modern education. This paper presents the design and development of a Music Teaching System based on the Android platform, aimed at providing an interactive, portable, and scalable solution for students and educators. The system architecture follows the B/S model and is developed using Java and Kotlin for Android Studio. It integrates core modules including music theory tutorials, instrument practice guidance, AI-based voice and pitch recognition, real-time feedback, and student performance analytics. A lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is embedded to evaluate pitch accuracy and rhythm synchronization in real-time during singing or instrument practice. The system was tested by 150 music learners over a period of 4 weeks. Results indicate a significant improvement in learning engagement (by 35%) and accuracy in pitch recognition (by 28%) compared to traditional app-less teaching approaches. The application also supports offline content access and cloud-based progress synchronization, making it suitable for both urban and rural learning contexts.

title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Music: A Review
authors: W. Ma; Z. Zheng
abstract: Crowd science is a science that uses the collective intelligence of information, physics, and society as a whole in the context of large-scale online interconnection to improve social and economic efficiency. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become an increasingly influential force in the field of music, reshaping traditional paradigms of creativity, production, performance, and consumption. This review examines the current applications of AI across key musical domains, including composition, audio production, performance, analysis, recommendation, and interdisciplinary integration. The paper highlights how AI techniques-ranging from symbolic rule-based systems to advanced deep learning architectures-have enabled novel capabilities such as automated melody and lyric generation, live collaboration between humans and AI agents in musical performance, sentiment-aware music analysis, and personalized recommendation systems. Additionally, the review explores the transformative effects of AI on the structure and ecology of the music industry, as well as its expanding role in education and therapy. Despite these advances, unresolved challenges remain in areas such as interpretability, ethical accountability, and the definition of creativity. The paper concludes by outlining future research directions, emphasizing the importance of human-AI collaboration, standardization of methodologies, and the development of adaptive AI systems for live musical contexts. By synthesizing recent progress and identifying open questions, this review provides a foundation for understanding the evolving relationship between AI and music.

authors: Y. -T. Yeh; Y. -H. Chen; Y. -C. Cheng; J. -T. Wu; J. -J. Fu; Y. -F. Yeh; Y. -H. Yang
abstract: Neural network models for guitar amplifier emulation, while being effective, often demand high computational cost and lack interpretability. title: Towards Explainable Music Emotion Recognition for Guitar Improvisations
authors: M. Rossi; D. Stefani; J. Pauwels; G. Iacca; L. Turchet
abstract: Explainability has gained significant attention across various domains, yet it remains relatively underexplored in the field of music, particularly in Music Emotion Recognition. This paper presents XMERApp; a web application designed to provide interpretability for a deep learning model that classifies classical and acoustic guitar into four emotional states. Our system employs a deep learning architecture trained on improvised musical performances to classify emotions, while providing comprehensive explainability through multiple complementary approaches. The application offers users three levels of interpretability: (1) detailed breakdowns of prediction probabilities across different emotion categories, enabling users to understand the confidence and uncertainty in model predictions; (2) temporal visualization of emotion evolution throughout the improvisation, revealing how the model’s understanding of emotional content develops over time; and (3) LIME-based explanations that highlight specific spectrogram regions most influential to the model’s decisions within focused time windows. Additionally, users can listen to the specific spectrogram regions identified as critical for the emotion classification, gaining insights into which parts of the performance and frequency ranges contributed the most to the model’s output. The web-based nature of XMERApp enables deployment across many devices, including smart musical instruments, enhancing the interpretability of intelligent features embedded within them.

title: Deep Learning-Powered Gesture and Speech Recognition in Augmented Reality Interfaces
authors: O. Kosimov; Y. Nurbek; O. Olimboy; A. Sharma; F. Jumaniyazova; F. Nurullayev
abstract: Augmented Reality (AR) interfaces demand intuitive and natural human-computer interaction modalities to enhance user experience and accessibility. Traditional AR input methods often rely on handheld controllers or touch-based interactions that can limit the immersive potential of AR applications. This research aims to develop and evaluate a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates gesture and speech recognition for seamless AR interface control. The methodology employs a hybrid architecture combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for real-time hand gesture recognition and Transformer-based models for continuous speech recognition, integrated through a fusion layer that processes multimodal inputs simultaneously. The system was trained on a custom dataset of 50,000 gesture samples and 100,000 speech utterances collected from 200 participants across diverse demographic groups. The experimental findings indicate that the suggested multimodal system attains 94.7 % in gesture recognition and 96.2 % in speech recognition and together they constitute 97.8 % accuracy where both modalities are exploited jointly. The framework is interactive with an average of 45ms latency and able to support real-time performance of AR applications. This study leads to the further development of the natural user interface in the AR context and has large-scale prospects and implications in the sphere of accessibility and productivity apps and immersive computing experience.

title: Expressive Acoustic Guitar Sound Synthesis with an Instrument-Specific Input Representation and Diffusion Outpainting
authors: H. Kim; S. Choi; J. Nam
abstract: Synthesizing performing guitar sound is a highly challenging task due to the polyphony and high variability in expression. Recently, deep generative models have shown promising results in synthesizing expressive polyphonic instrument sounds from music scores, often using a generic MIDI input. In this work, we propose an expressive acoustic guitar sound synthesis model with a customized input representation to the instrument, which we call guitarroll. We implement the proposed approach using diffusion-based outpainting which can generate audio with long-term consistency. To overcome the lack of MIDI/audio-paired datasets, we used not only an existing guitar dataset but also collected data from a high quality sample-based guitar synthesizer. Through quantitative and qualitative evaluations, we show that our proposed model has higher audio quality than the baseline model and generates more realistic timbre sounds than the previous leading work.

title: An Experimental Study on the Effect of AI Voice Prominence on Users’ Emotional Responses
authors: Y. -R. Chang; C. -W. Cheng
abstract: This study investigates the impact of AI voice prominence on emotional responses across various digital content contexts. Using three levels of voice prominence—high (e.g., podcasts), medium (e.g., travel vlogs), and low (e.g., background vocals in Instagram posts)— the authors evaluated 39 university students' reactions with the Self-Assessment Manikin (SAM) scale. ANOVA results show that lower voice prominence increases pleasure and arousal, while voice prominence was not found to be significantly related to dominance. Interviews revealed that acceptance is shaped by AI voice naturalness, contextual appropriateness, and emotional relevance. AI voices were more acceptable in humorous or informational content but less preferred in emotionally expressive formats. title: Utilizing Generative AI to Develop Programming Skill Through Self-Directed and Interactive Learning
authors: N. Puttajanyawong; W. Suamuang; K. Chomsuwan
abstract: In an era where technology plays a significant role in the lives of people of all ages, adapting to rapidly advancing technology is essential. Lifelong learning, which integrates formal, non-formal, and informal education, helps learners develop skills and abilities independently. Programming skills serve as an example of lifelong learning, requiring the development of technical skills such as programming, planning, and testing, as well as communication, teamwork, and systematic thinking. This research focuses on utilizing Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) to enhance programming skills through self-directed learning combined with interactive learning. The study was conducted with 21 students enrolled in the Higher Vocational Certificate (Diploma) program in Mechatronics and Robotics. The study applied the MAR model, which consists of three stages: The motivation stage, is designed to encourage learners to engage in activities that link prior knowledge or experiences with new knowledge, thereby fostering self-directed learning motivation, such as designing personalized learning activities based on individual interests; the Activity stage, which provides opportunities for learners to use Generative AI technology for self-directed learning according to their goals and plans, enabling them to understand concepts, apply knowledge in various situations, and track their learning progress; and the Reflection and Progress stage, focusing on reviewing, analyzing, and reflecting on learning outcomes, as well as exchanging ideas and skills with peers and receiving constructive feedback. These stages were designed based on theoretical foundations and a literature review. Furthermore, the research emphasized ethical considerations in AI use, such as data privacy and societal impacts, to promote high-quality, beneficial lifelong learning. The findings showed that before the learning process, the learner had no background in programming and had never used AI technology. However, after participating in the learning activities, students became more open to learning and responded positively to the self-designed activities, which aligned with their interests and skills related to their field of study. These findings suggest that this learning process, when implemented effectively, can be applied to lifelong learning for individuals of all genders and ages.

title: Musical Instrument Recognition Using Machine Learning Approaches
authors: C. B. K; B. K. N; K. Puttegowda; M. A. V; S. K. D. S; A. K; Y. G. R
abstract: This work focuses on musical instrument recognition in miscellaneous audio sources, a fundamental issue of the machine auditory system. We contrast traditional machine learning techniques against deep learning strategies in a clinical dataset solved under a supervised multi-label, multi-output classification paradigm. To enhance the performance of the system, we adjust the analysis parameters for window size, hop size, and label threshold levels. Furthermore, we explore the benefits of auxiliary feature sets as alternative data representations, specifically: Auditory features are based on two categories: (1) four-band spectral decomposition of stereo sound data, left, right, mid, and side channels and (2) the harmonic and residual model of the audio signal. Two methods for fusing the models trained on these representations are suggested and we use the best of these methods to increase recognition accuracy. These enhancements lead to a vast improvement; with a 14.25 % increase M-F score for the macro average and a 24.17 % improvement in the exact match ratio overall compared to the baseline.

title: Deep Learning Techniques for Weed Detection in Agricultural Environments: A Comprehensive Review
authors: D. G. Pai; R. Kamath; M. Balachandra
abstract: Agriculture has been completely transformed by Deep Learning (DL) techniques, which allow for quick object localization and detection. However, because weeds and crops are similar in color, form, and texture, weed detection and categorization can be difficult. Advantages in object detection, recognition, and image classification can be obtained with deep learning (DL), a vital aspect of machine learning (ML). Because crops and weeds are similar, ML techniques have difficulty extracting and choosing distinguishing traits. This literature review demonstrates the potential of various DL methods for crop weed identification, localization, and classification. This research work investigates the present status of Deep Learning based weed identification and categorization systems. The majority of research employs supervised learning strategies, polishing pre-trained models on sizable, labeled datasets to achieve high accuracy. Innovations are driven by the need for sustainable weed management methods, and deep learning is demonstrating encouraging outcomes in image-based weed detection systems. To solve issues like resource scarcity, population increase, and climate change, precision agriculture holds great promise for the integration of AI with IoT-enabled farm equipment.
