title: A Novel Voice-Processing Method Leveraging Polyphonic Audio for Instrument Recognition Using Machine Learning
authors: S. Telsang; T. Phad; M. Pingale; P. Singh; A. Pillay; P. Lohar; M. Pilgonde; P. Raj
abstract: In this research, a novel polyphonic voice recognition system for instrument identification, pitch detection, and chord detection based on machine learning techniques is presented. The system utilizes python and its large set of data analytics libraries to provide efficient and realistic audio recognition. Some of the main techniques involve Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) for feature extraction and classification models like $k$-nearest neighbors ($k-N N$) and hidden Markov models (hmm). MFCC s have been used to efficiently extract the spectral features of the audio signals, whereas K-NN classifiers ($k=3$) and hmm models (8 gaussian states) yield high instrument identification and sequential pattern audio analysis. The system also presents high accuracies of 58% using K-NN and 67% using hmm in classifying 8 instruments namely acoustic guitar, bass drum, cello, clarinet, double bass, flute, hi hat, saxophone, snare drum, violin. A stratified shuffle split strategy and a balanced dataset guarantee fair training and testing. The frontend, coded in html, CSS, and JavaScript, supports dynamic audio visualization and easy user interaction through web audio Api, whereas the backend, implemented with python and flask, processes real-time audio and machine learning operations. Iterative feedback-based updates enhance system flexibility even further, which makes it worthwhile for use in music education, production, transcription, and research applications. In spite of difficulties in overlapping sound separation and intricate polyphonic audio analysis, this research emphasizes the revolutionary potential of intelligent audio processing in developing music technology.

title: Detection of AI-Generated vs. Real Human Images Using Anatomical Subregions (Hands, Eyes, Nose) with Image Processing and Deep Learning
authors: C. Buangam; M. Phaiphon; N. Jewmungme; P. Worrawichaipat
abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has enabled the creation of highly realistic human images, raising concerns about identity fraud, misinformation, and other security risks. Distinguishing real from AI-generated content is increasingly difficult with the human eye alone.In this work, we first contribute a structured dataset of cropped anatomical subregions – hands, eyes, and noses – comprising both real images from public sources and synthetic images generated by diffusion models. Using this dataset, we develop deep learning classifiers (CNN, EfficientNet-B0, and ResNet50) to distinguish real and synthetic images. To further investigate model performance, we introduce two preprocessing variations – vignetting and edge enhancement – in addition to plain images, and compare their impact across different architectures.Our evaluation shows that ResNet50 trained on plain images achieves the highest accuracy, reaching 87.66% for hands, 95.61% for eyes, and 95.36% for noses. Finally, we ensemble the best-performing subgroup classifiers into a random forest decision-maker, which achieves an overall accuracy of 97%. This work contributes both a curated anatomical dataset and a multi-model detection pipeline, offering practical tools to address the growing challenges of AI-generated media.

title: SoundRubric: Musical Performance Analysis for Violin Learning Using Audio Deconstruction
authors: A. Arora
abstract: This paper outlines a framework for evaluating violin performance by deconstructing musical elements in audio form. An evaluative rubric based on nine selective parameters is created to evaluate performances and assess them for pitch accuracy, rhythm consistency, intonation, dynamic detail, temporal stability, harmonic complexity, and duration accuracy. By using empirical analysis on self-recorded violin performances, a deconstructive system was designed that allows users to see how their audio compares to original reference song files using various signal processing methods including dynamic time warping (DTW), chroma feature extraction, and waveform deviation analysis. The results of evaluation were synthesized into personal summarized feedback using large language models and allowed real-time feedback to be delivered through the application called SoundRubric. The results demonstrate that the multi-dimensional analysis provided accurate and actionable feedback and represents a substantial leap forward for scalable low-cost and intelligent music education.

title: Recognition and Error Correction of Piano Playing Music based on Spatial Attention Mechanism with Convolutional Neural Network
authors: J. Zhao; K. Yu
abstract: This Nowadays, piano education industry has developed significantly which captures large share in market and reflects enhancing demand for piano learning and music education. However, automatic estimation function of piano performance has inadequacies in piano education. The Spatial Attention Mechanism with Convolutional Neural Network (SAM-CNN) is proposed for piano playing music for recognition and error correction. The SAM-CNN enhances the recognition accuracy through integrating spatial attention and focus on significant part of input data at classification which leads to better handling and complex music patterns. The CNN extracts feature like notes, rhythm patterns from preprocessed data and identifies most significant data for music recognition. The median filter was applied to smooth the input through removing noises and reserving significant data features which is helpful for accurate musical pattern recognition. The SAM-CNN performance is measured with metrics of precision, accuracy and recall. The SAM-CNN attains 97.76% precision, 98.57% accuracy and 98.12% recall for Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) dataset which is superior than Fuzzy Neural Network (FNN).

title: An Error Correction Model for Piano Teaching Based on Improved Endpoint Detection with CNN-HMM
authors: S. Chen
abstract: Piano teaching is based on teaching performance skills, which is an important practical discipline for interactive and personalized teaching. In order to realize the automation and digital teaching of piano, and to improve the level of piano performance and aesthetic effect, the research firstly uses the endpoint detection technology to realize the temporal value detection of the audio data, and then integrates the convolutional neural network and the Hidden Markov Model for the extraction and recognition of the note events, and finally completes the transcription of the piano audio and the correction of the errors. The research-designed piano teaching aid error correction method is conducive to improving the efficiency and quality of piano teaching, and provides an effective reference for the application of artificial intelligence in the field of music education.

title: Graph Neural Network Empowers Intelligent Education: A Systematic Review From an Application Perspective
authors: C. He; J. Luo; Y. Tang; G. Chen; Q. Guan
abstract: Intelligent education, also known as education driven by artificial intelligence (AI), has emerged as a research hot spot. AI technologies can empower various intelligent education applications, such as learning behaviors analysis and adaptive learning. In recent years, graph neural network (GNN), as an advanced AI technology, has demonstrated its superiority in extracting insights from graph-structured data. It also has attracted significant attention in the field of intelligent education, where graph-structured data are ubiquitous (e.g., student/teacher collaboration networks). Although previous review studies have explored the applications of GNNs in some fields, there has been limited discussion on their specific applications and potential in intelligent education. To fill this gap, we collected 85 representative studies on GNN applications in intelligent education and conducted a systematical review through the bibliometric analysis. This review uncovers three key findings: 1) benefiting from the vigorous promotion by Chinese scholars, GNN applications in intelligent education have demonstrated a remarkable growth over the past six years; 2) various GNNs have been extensively utilized across six pivotal application scenarios: learner modeling, learning performance prediction, learning resource recommendation, intelligent teaching assistance, classroom behavior analysis, and educational emotion analysis, all of which have exhibited high performance; and 3) despite notable challenges, research on GNN empowering intelligent education still has many promising directions, such as enhancing interpretability, integrating multimodal educational data, collaborating with a large language model, and expanding more applications.

title: Enhancing College Students’ Achievement, Motivation, and Engagement in Film Character Design Through AI-Driven Smart Sketchpad: A Personalized Interactive Learning Model for Art Education
authors: S. Zeng; N. Rahim; S. Xu
abstract: As technologies such as artificial intelligence rapidly evolve, the traditional lecture-based class can no longer meet students’ learning needs. Previous research has demonstrated that AI can be essential for improving the learning experience. However, research has also pointed out that promoting AI applications in education has been challenging. Developing domain-specific applications based on AI technology is a massive challenge for the development of AI in education. Further research has pointed out that the development of AI applications in education rarely considers students’ perceptual learning motivations. This study proposes a teaching method based on an artificial intelligence tool, the Artificial Intelligence Smart Sketchpad (AISS), to assist in teaching character art design in a multimedia environment. The artificial intelligence will identify students’ drawing sketches and make corrections. This study explores the impact of AISS on achievement, engagement, and motivation among film character art design students in a multimedia environment. To this end, we adopted a quantitative research method. Over five weeks, we assessed 60 university students. Research results indicate that the AI smart sketchpad (AISS) significantly improves students’ motivation, engagement, and performance. Student feedback suggests that AI stimulates creative thinking by offering greater creative freedom and possibilities and quickly transforming sketches into high-quality design drawings. A new direction will be explored for personalized and self-learning for students.

title: Cloud Network Anomaly Detection Using Machine and Deep Learning Techniques— Recent Research Advancements
authors: A. M. Abdallah; A. Saif Rashed Obaid Alkaabi; G. Bark Nasser Douman Alameri; S. H. Rafique; N. S. Musa; T. Murugan
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of computing and networking, the concepts of cloud networks have gained significant prominence. Although the cloud network offers on-demand access to shared resources, anomalies pose potential risks to the integrity and security of cloud networks. However, protecting the cloud network against anomalies remains a challenge. Unlike traditional detection techniques, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) offer new and adaptable methods for detecting anomalies in cloud networks. The objective of this study is to comprehensively explore existing ML /DL methods for detecting different anomalies based on distributed denial of service anomaly (DDoS) and intrusion detection systems (IDS) in cloud networks. The study seeks to address the gaps in anomaly detection for cloud networks, proposing potential solutions for anomaly detection in these cloud environments. The ultimate goal is to contribute valuable insights and practical solutions to enhance the security and reliability of cloud networks through effective anomaly detection by ML/ DL techniques. Methodologies for ML/DL are explained, along with their advantages, disadvantages, and respective approaches. In addition, a summary of the comparison between different ML/ DL models is also included.

title: Automatic Detection and Analysis of Singing Mistakes for Music Learning by Imitation
authors: S. Kumar; S. Jaiswal; P. Singh; V. Arora
abstract: The advancement of machine learning in audio analysis has opened new possibilities for technology-enhanced music education. This paper introduces a framework for automatic singing mistake detection in the context of Indian Art Music (IAM) pedagogy, supported by a newly curated dataset. The dataset comprises synchronized teacher–learner vocal recordings collected in an imitation-learning setting, with annotations indicating teacher-identified learner mistakes. Using this dataset, we develop different deep learning models for frame-level detection of frequency and amplitude mistakes and benchmark them against a rule-based approach. To compare the efficacy of the mistake detection system, a new evaluation methodology is proposed. A systematic study of errors and cross-teacher analysis reveals inherent subjectivity in annotation practices, indicating that music pedagogy is personalized and shaped by individual teacher-specific evaluation and annotation criteria. The findings offer valuable insights into music pedagogy, with implications for the design of more robust, interpretable, and pedagogically aligned music analysis systems. title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Integration in Teacher Education in China
authors: D. Wang; H. Wu
abstract: This thesis presents a bibliometric analysis of the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in teacher education, utilizing CiteSpace software to explore academic publications in the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) which is the most influential academic database in China. With the rapid development of AI technologies and their potential impact on education, this study aims to systematically map the evolution of AI in teacher education research within the Chinese academic context. By analyzing a comprehensive dataset of published articles, the study identifies key trends, research hotspots, and emerging themes in the field. The bibliometric indicators, such as publication frequency, citation patterns, co-authorship networks, and keyword co-occurrence, are examined to reveal the scholarly landscape and to track the growth of AI -related educational research. The findings highlight the major contributors to the field, the development trajectory of AI in teacher training, and the collaboration networks that shape this growing domain. Additionally, this research offers insights into the challenges and opportunities that AI presents to teacher education in China, suggesting directions for future research and policy development. Overall, the study underscores the importance of AI integration in shaping the future of teacher education and provides a framework for understanding its impact through bibliometric analysis.

title: Using AI Techniques for Building Personalized LMS Learning Modules
authors: F. Schimanke; B. Ruf
abstract: With the release of ChatGPT, Pandora's box of generative AI has been opened, and the new technology is here to stay. This also impacts academic education, where it bears certain challenges while also providing new opportunities. Students and educators alike will have to adapt to the newly available technology and find ways to use it in meaningful and profitable way. One way to make good use of generative AI in the classroom is to build personalized learning environments for students that adapt to their individual progress and enhance the learning process with technologies that are tailored to the modern students. In the presented work, two of these technologies and the concept of spaced repetition are used to build a personalized learning module within the learning management system LMS “ILIAS”. One of the used tools is an AI chatbot based on the ChatGPT API that is trained on the lecturer's actual course materials and enhanced with answers from ChatGPT itself. The other technology improves educational videos by providing learners with a button to pause the video at any time and to receive additional explanations about the content currently discussed, while considering the context of the entire video so far. These two AI tools are then provided in combination with a spaced repetition algorithm, which creates a personal learning environment that is highly tailored to the individual learners' needs.

title: Brain Tumor Classification in MRI: Insights From LIME and Grad-CAM Explainable AI Techniques
authors: H. C. Yoon; L. P. Lin
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly vital in brain tumour diagnosis using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). This study serves as a reproduction and interpretability case study, evaluating the behaviour of established convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures: VGG16, ResNet50, and EfficientNet through the implementation of Explainable AI (XAI) to interpret their black-box predictions of tumour classes. All models were trained with early stopping, achieving high classification accuracy: VGG16 and ResNet50 exceeded 98%, while EfficientNetB0 achieved 96%; however, misclassification between Glioma and Meningioma remains a challenge, suggesting overlapping features. VGG16 exhibited more stable validation accuracy; ResNet50 demonstrated fluctuations due to its deeper architecture and broader feature activations, while EfficientNet maintained a more gradual learning curve, attributed to its compound scaling. To enhance interpretability, Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) and Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) were applied. LIME segments images into superpixels and analyses their contributions through repeated perturbations. LIME revealed that CNNs sometimes relied on irrelevant background features, including brain edges and anatomical distractions, leading to misclassification. Meanwhile, Grad-CAM, which highlights class-discriminative regions through gradient-based heatmaps, demonstrated key architectural differences: ResNet50 activated broader spatial areas, VGG16 focused on more localized tumour features, while EfficientNet often considered wider anatomical contexts that extended to structures such as eye sockets and the nasal cavity. These results underscore how architectural depth and feature aggregation influence classification performance and reveal potential limitations in CNN-based classification. This study contributes a comparative interpretability perspective, demonstrating how architecture-specific behaviours influence feature attribution and reliability in CNN-based brain tumour classification.

title: Evaluation of Deep Learning Approaches for Pitch Scoring in Piano Practice and Performance
authors: J. Mekkoktanphira; P. Pangwapee; N. Dilokthanakul; S. Lochanachit; P. Pavarangkoon; N. Kanungsukkasem
abstract: This study evaluates deep learning approaches for pitch scoring in piano practice and performance through two experiments. The first experiment compares Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) and Transformer architectures using datasets that include diverse musical elements such as pitch, rhythm, rest, and tempo. The results demonstrate that Transformers significantly outperform GRUs in terms of accuracy and robustness across all conditions. The second experiment investigates modifications to the Transformer model, specifically increasing the number of attention heads, to assess its impact on transcribing musical sequences of varying complexity. title: Construction of Personalized Music Theory Teaching Model in Colleges and Universities: Machine Learning Perspective
authors: Y. Tao; Z. Li; C. Yu
abstract: In colleges and universities, music theory courses often adopt uniform teaching methods that fail to consider students' varying backgrounds, skill levels, and learning interests. This study proposes a personalized music theory teaching model from a machine learning. Using datasets of 400 students from Jisou University, the model first applied logistic regression to predict students' mastery of music theory with a precision of 0.89. Subsequently, $K$-means clustering ($K=3$) identified three optimal learning profiles-Achiever, Explorer, and Expressive-that guided differentiated teaching strategies. Furthermore, model employed the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to evaluate the teaching outcomes from multiple dimensions. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with the traditional teaching model, the personalized teaching model increased teaching evaluation scores by 25% and 27% for freshmen and sophomores, respectively. Average test scores also improved by 4.4 and 6 points. These findings demonstrate that the model not only enhances the effectiveness of music theory teaching but also provides a replicable framework for integrating machine learning into college-level music education.

title: A Subjective Evaluation Dataset for GuitarSet
authors: T. Hojo; Y. Sugiura; N. Yasui; T. Shimamura
abstract: In this paper, we create and evaluate a dataset of subjective evaluation for acoustic guitar performances. The study uses audio clips divided into four-measure segments from the GuitarSet. As evaluation criteria, we adopt ASR (Acoustic Satisfaction Rating), which assesses four items on a five-point scale: discomfort of the sound, variation in picking intensity, onset deviation from the metronome, and offset deviation from the metronome. We conducted an online subjective evaluation experiment with 84 crowd workers to calculate the Mean Opinion Score (MOS). After data screening, the ICC3K exceeded 0.50, demonstrating the dataset’s reliability. For validation, we tested the dataset’s suitability for a deep learning approach by using a Transformer model that takes four-measure guitar performance audio as input and outputs MOS. In the evaluation experiment, the model exhibited low SROCC and PLCC values. These results indicate that human perceptual evaluation of guitar performances is highly complex and challenging to model.

abstract: Reinforcement learning algorithm is a kind of machine learning method that constantly adjusts its behavior through trial and error to maximize long-term cumulative rewards, which can provide personalized instruction for music learners. title: Piano Music Style Analysis and Recognition Based on Deep Learning
authors: S. Luo
abstract: In response to the problems of multi instrument signal interference, insufficient capture of piano specific features, and weak collaborative modeling of long-term structures and local details in existing piano music style recognition, this study proposes a complete technical solution of “multi-source data processing multi-dimensional feature engineering adaptive deep learning model”. The research first uses optical score recognition, MIDI track screening, and audio preprocessing techniques to achieve score recognition MIDI、 Standardized integration of three types of piano audio data to eliminate non piano signal interference and data distribution differences; Next, extract piano specific acoustic features that cover key pressure and pedal effects, as well as musicological features that include harmonic conversion frequency and rhythm complexity, to construct a two-dimensional feature system; Finally, a recognition model is designed based on a dual layer bidirectional long short-term memory network (Bi LSTM) and attention mechanism, dynamically focusing on core distinguishing features of different styles to improve modeling accuracy. The experiment used 6 types of piano style data as samples, and the results showed that the proposed model achieved an accuracy of 92.3% on the test set, with a macro average F1 of 89.6%, significantly better than traditional machine learning models and basic deep learning models. At the same time, it revealed the musicological nature of style confusion, providing an effective technical path for piano music style recognition and supporting practical applications such as piano teaching and automatic classification of music libraries.

title: 1D CNN-Based Traditional Instrument Classification and Notation Generation in Sinhala for Gataberaya and Flute
authors: P. G. R. Dulmi; B. Hettige
abstract: Applications for traditional musical instruments from Sri Lanka have not received enough attention, even with the progress in machine learning. This paper presents a novel method for categorizing and transcribing notations for the flute and gataberaya which is an indigenous drum from Sri Lanka using deep learning methods. Based on a manually recorded audio recording dataset with 168 flute recordings and 81 gataberaya recordings with varying lengths and single-noted, 1D Convolutional Neural Networks were used to construct a classification model. The system also generates musical notations from audio recordings using an algorithm and converts Western musical notation to Sinhala musical notations using a prompt with a Large Language Model API call. The methodology includes data augmentation for raw data and feature extraction with Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients, and frequency analysis using the Fast Fourier Transform. The classification model achieved 88.71% training accuracy and 91.16% validation accuracy, successfully identifying instrument types, and the notation generation for the flute shows effectiveness by correctly recognizing the notes and the relative octave of the frequency. However, challenges remain for unpitched instruments like the Gataberaya due to the limited dataset. This approach acts as a valuable tool for the preservation of Sri Lankan traditional music.

title: Piano-Assisted Practice System Based on Multi-Tone Using Attention-Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Network
authors: Y. Zhang
abstract: In an audio practice system considered for multi-tone exercises, users engage with a variety of pitch and tone patterns to increase their auditory discrimination and musical skills. However, a music learner does not select a piece to play without an accurate evaluation according to present level. This issue is extremely complicated because of its data scarcity and subjectivity. In this research, the Attention-Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Network (ATT-MSCNN) is proposed for a piano-assisted practice system based on multitone performance. Initially, Yingcai Piano Performance Evaluation Phase III Dataset (YCU-PPE-III) is used to evaluate proposed approach performance. The Constant-Q Transform (CQT), z-score normalization, and window approaches are applied in pre-processing stage. Then, the Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) is used to extract the audio features. Finally, ATT-MSCNN is performed for a piano-assisted practice system. The ATT-MSCNN achieves a better accuracy of 99.43% compared to existing approaches like ResNet, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and MSCNN.

title: Intelligent-Translation Adaptive Learning System for Ideological and Political Teaching of Translation Specialized Courses
authors: Y. Zhang
abstract: From the past few years, ideological and political education (IPE) has developed as a key component of translation Courses pedagogy, directing to incorporate moral cultivation with linguistic skill development. However, traditional models mainly rely on manual classroom teaching, static theoretical instruction and qualitative evaluation which restricts flexibility and measurable assessment. To overcome these challenges, this research proposes an Intelligent-Translation Adaptive Learning System (ITALS) that applies Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) to attain data-driven IPE and Translation Courses incorporation. Initially, bilingual translation texts, classroom interaction records and reflective essays were gathers and normalized via semantic processing and feature tagging to confirm contextual consistency. Then, the NLP module examined both translation accuracy to create feature embeddings. After that, the RL-based adaptive engine dynamically adjusted instructional content and delivered personalized learning recommendations based on performance feedback. Finally, the proposed ITALS model formed automated translation evaluations and ideological and political comprehension score for every individual learner. Experimental results established that the proposed ITALS model attained greater results in precision 0.98 compared to existing Constructivist-Intercultural Translation Integration (CITI) model.

title: Data Driven Insight for AI Music E-Learning: Churn Prediction and Behavioral Segmentation
authors: H. D. Wirasti; H. Fakhrurroja; O. N. Pratiwi
abstract: This study presents a data science and analytics-driven evaluation of AI-based e-learning platforms for music education, focusing on user churn prediction and behavioral segmentation. Using an open-access dataset from Yousician, which includes 30-day activity logs from 1,000 ukulele learners, the research applies ten machine learning classifiers to predict churn and leverages SHAP values for model interpretability. Gradient Boosting achieved the best balance between precision $(0.75)$, recall (0.94), and F1-score (0.83). Additionally, K-Means clustering combined with Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was employed to identify distinct learner segments among churned and non-churned users. The resulting clusters inform differentiated marketing strategies and user retention interventions. Business impact analysis shows a $\mathbf{1 0 0. 7 \%}$ increase in monthly revenue after applying predictive and clustering models. This framework demonstrates the potential of integrating predictive analytics and unsupervised learning to support personalized feedback, targeted re-engagement, and strategic decision-making in digital music education platforms.

title: Multi-Track Audio Fusion for Emotion Recognition Using Machine and Deep Learning Techniques
authors: J. Banerjee; M. Ahmad; T. Tabassum
abstract: Emotion recognition from audio signals is essential for human-computer interaction, affective computing, and mental health monitoring. However, traditional single-track systems often fail to capture the full range of emotional nuance in complex audio environments. Motivated by this challenge, we propose a multi-track audio fusion-based approach to improve emotion classification accuracy. Using Bangla song recordings, we extract Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, spectral, and temporal features, then apply feature-level fusion to build enriched audio representations. These features are classified using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and compared against classical machine learning models, including SVM, RF, and CatBoost. The CNN model achieved superior performance, with a 99.45% accuracy rate on multi-emotion classification. Our results confirm the robustness of multi-track fusion and deep learning in building more precise and scalable emotion recognition systems.

title: Design of Music Art Teaching Quality Evaluation System Based on Deep Convolution Neural Network Algorithm
authors: F. Lin; T. Gu; W. Liu
abstract: Art teaching is an art subject with strong practicality. Its teaching philosophy focuses on improving students’ musical knowledge, cultivating students’ musical singing ability and deepening students’ artistic aesthetic sentiment. Exploring a new teaching mode of music art major in colleges and universities has become an important issue that music educators in colleges and universities pay attention to. In this paper, based on the deep convolution neural network algorithm, the teaching quality of music art is further studied. The research shows that CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) is the first to achieve basic convergence. When the training rounds are 40, it has reached basic convergence, and the accuracy of the verification set can reach $65 \%$. And when the training rounds of AI (Artificial intelligence) are 70 and 60, the basic convergence of AI is achieved, and the accuracy of verification set is $58 \%$ and $60 \%$. title: Evaluation Singing Art Voice Quality Using Siamese Gated Recurrent Extreme Learning Networks
authors: Y. Dong
abstract: The quick evolution of artificial intelligence and deep learning has provided new chances for singing art voice quality assessment, where exact evaluation of the vocal performance is critical to training, music education, and intelligent feedback systems. Current methods tend to depend on hand-engineered acoustic features, rule-based processing, or shallow machine learning models that do not handle intricate temporal-spectral dependencies present in singing signals and exhibit weak generalization and weak adaptability to varied voice types. Conventional methods like MFCC-based classification, simple CNN architectures, and recurrent networks have demonstrated some progress but are faced with high computation, overfitting, and inadequate robust attention mechanisms. To cope with the above challenges, a Siamese Gated Recurrent Extreme Learning Networks (SGRELN) is proposed by incorporating gated recurrent units, extreme learning machines and Siamese modules for emphasizing prominent vocal features. Experimental results clearly show noteworthy superiority, where RAT-CNN attains 98.8% accuracy and 97.7 % F1-score compared to traditional models. Comparative mechanism emphasizes the efficacy, strength, and interpretability of the model proposed, with greater reliability in real applications of singing quality evaluation in the real world with superior performance, scalability, and domain adaptability.

title: Strumming in the Metaverse: A Deep-Learning-Enabled Virtual Air Guitar System in VR With Enhanced Chord Recognition and Simulated Pedal Effects
authors: Y. -Z. Hsieh; J. -J. Lin; M. -C. Su; W. -J. Lin
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly capable and inexpensive, and VR devices have become indispensable in many domains, such as gaming, videoconferencing, education, and healthcare. VR has also been applied to music performance and learning. Virtual instruments, such as virtual pianos and drums, free users from the need to own physical forms of these (often bulky and expensive) instruments. VR devices enable users to enjoy music anytime and anywhere without constraints. Virtual concerts, including spatial audio simulations and reconstructions of historical performances, are becoming increasingly common. Previous studies have primarily examined virtual guitars in non-VR environments and air guitar chord recognition. However, systematic research on virtual air guitar systems in VR remains scarce. Virtual guitar games that are available on the market cannot recognize hand gestures accurately and thus cannot accurately identify the strumming patterns and chords played by the player. To overcome this problem, we propose a VR-based virtual air guitar system that can recognize 30 chords and various strumming techniques through deep learning and visual feedback. Employing a black-box approach, we combine WaveNet and FiLM to simulate electric guitar pedal effects with a knob difference loss mechanism, which simulates the turning of knobs on a guitar effects pedal, for enhanced accuracy.

title: Study a deep learning-based audio classification for detecting the distance of UAV
authors: D. Utebayeva; A. Yembergenova
abstract: Recently, drones have become widely used in almost everyday life and at many crowded events due to their versatility. There were incidents involving them, both intentional and unintentional. One of the most essential studies of preventing drone occurrences could involve evaluating the recognition of their distance to people and protected areas. The potential performance of deep learning methods in the field of recognition has led to motivation to explore the distances of UAVs based on their sounds. Therefore, this study examined a deep learning method based on Gated Reccurent Unit (GRU) to study the classification capability of drone sounds, particularly the classification capability of drone sounds flying at different distances. So, we tried to study whether the sound classification method has the ability to recognize drone flights at different distances. During our experimental tests, drones were launched at intervals of every five meters from ground level. According to experimental studies, drone sounds can be recognized from a distance of every 10 meters or more, and the average recognition accuracy in such tasks can be 94-98 percent. Such a system can be offered into a complex recognition system, which can be inserted as a functional part of bimodal and multi-modal systems.

title: Machine Learning Approaches for Musical Instrument Recognition using Distinctive Audio Features
authors: B. R; A. M B
abstract: Automatic musical instrument recognition, being part of the machine listening, is an important task. In this work, we are concerned with instrument recognition for multi-instrument. In this work, the goal will be to consider different approaches to classification of signal containing audio data in music. Main objectives of this work included the understanding of how various features make two or more instrumental sounds unique, the identification of how these features can be extracted in the most effective matter and the final one was to study and to identify the type of the instrument mostly playing in a specific musical file with the help of suitable Machine learning algorithms. This study proved that the proposal to identify the pre-dominant instrument of a song is plausible with the help of machine learning techniques. This work contributes to the field of automatic musical instrument recognition by focusing on the classification of multi-instrument audio signals. It offers a practical framework to identify and analyze features that can distinguish instrumental sounds and how to extract and use these features together with appropriate machine learning algorithms to detect the main instrument in audio files. Based on the study, it is found that it is possible to selectively identify the principal instrument in a song, which requires only a big amount of time and the efficient machine learning approaches used in the research offer a high level of accuracy. Considering the presented results, it becomes clear that spectral features concern instrument timbre discriminability and are important to the classification process. In the context of the proposed method, it was possible to achieve nearly 91% accuracy in identifying whole families of instruments and particular instruments belonging to these families, which proves the effectiveness of the stated approach.

title: Intelligent Feedback for Sports Training Using UAV Swarms Based on Transformer and Reinforcement Learning
authors: Z. Zhu
abstract: To address the limitations of traditional fixed-position camera systems in capturing wide-range and multi-angle motion data during athletic training, this study proposes and constructs an intelligent real-time feedback system powered by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV). Leveraging the mobility of UAV swarms, the system captures macroscopic actions and spatial trajectories of athletes in open environments from multiple aerial perspectives, thereby acquiring comprehensive motion data that conventional methods often miss. The system first employs a Spatio-Temporal Transformer (ST-Transformer) to model human skeletal keypoint sequences for precise action recognition and dynamic assessment. A Variational Autoencoder is then used to learn the distribution of an athlete’s optimal performance, enabling the construction of a personalized “ideal model” for real-time deviation analysis and anomaly detection. Finally, a Proximal Policy Optimization algorithm is used to train an agent capable of generating optimal feedback instructions based on real-time states, achieving adaptive guidance. System performance is evaluated using the NTU RGB+D 120 dataset (https://paperswithcode.com/dataset/ntu-rgb-d-120)and the UAV-Humandataset (https://github.com/sutdcv/UAV-Human). Results show that the proposed model achieves an action recognition accuracy of 95.2% on the NTU RGB+D 120 dataset, significantly outperforming the Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (ST-GCN) baseline. To further validate the model’s effectiveness under realistic UAV perspectives, testing on the UAV-Human dataset yields an action recognition accuracy exceeding 90%, again outperforming the re-implemented ST-GCN baseline (accuracy: 82.1%). Additionally, the system reaches a processing speed of 35 frames per second, meeting the stringent latency requirements of real-time feedback systems. These results compellingly demonstrate that the proposed model not only performs well under ideal conditions but also effectively handles practical challenges such as dynamic viewpoints, small target scales, and complex backgrounds in UAV footage. The proposed framework successfully integrates UAV-based dynamic visual sensing with advanced algorithmic analysis, forming a complete intelligent loop from precise perception and personalized diagnosis to adaptive guidance. This approach presents a novel, scientific, and efficient paradigm for real-time instruction in modern sports training.

title: Voice Type Classification in Choirs Using Acoustic Analysis Techniques
authors: G. C. Tahar; W. Hartanto; A. A. S. Gunawan; R. C. Pradana
abstract: To achieve the best vocal harmony in music, it is important to identify a person's vocal type, especially in a choir. Male (baritone, tenor, bass) and female (soprano, alto, mezzo-soprano) voice types can be used to categorize the distinctive vocal qualities of each choir member. This research proposes an acoustic analysis-based method that uses feature extraction techniques such as Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) and pitch analysis to extract a person's vocal characteristics to achieve accurate classification. A person's vocal type in a choir is then determined by analyzing these characteristics. The system classifies data using machine learning algorithms, specifically convolutional and artificial neural networks. The goal of the research is to create a system that can accurately and automatically recognize different types of voices in a choir. The experimental results show that the system can classify vocal types based on acoustic features with an accuracy of at least $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$, marking a significant advancement in music sound analysis.

title: Toward Accessible Auditory Health: A Cloud-Based fNIRS Solution for Auditory Training and Assessment
authors: Q. Huang; J. Liu; Y. Li; L. Zhao; K. Stawarz; H. Liu
abstract: Auditory training (AT) is a proactive intervention for managing auditory health and preventing hearing loss. However, in its current form, it requires significant financial and time resources. As the excellent performance of functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) in the medical field has led to its gradual application in auditory health, we aim to combine machine learning with fNIRS data to enhance accessibility and general applicability of AT. In this study, fNIRS was used to collect brain data related to auditory tasks and six machine learning methods were applied to classify different AT outcomes. Among these algorithms, AdaBoost demonstrated the best performance, achieving an accuracy of 88%. Based on the results, we propose a novel cloud-based framework that integrates AT with the assessment of training outcomes for individuals with hearing loss. The framework has been validated for its generalizability, and the evaluation results are not influenced by subjective experience.

title: Position Paper: Collectionless Artificial Intelligence
authors: M. Gori; S. Melacci
abstract: Storing and handling huge data collections has become the fundamental player in the progress of Machine Learning and of its spectacular results. However, learning from such data collections introduces risks related to data centralization, privacy, energy efficiency, limited customizability, and control. This paper sustains the position that the time has come for thinking of new learning protocols where machines conquer cognitive skills by online learning from potentially lifelong streams of sensory data, without the privilege of recording the temporal stream. The perspective of what we refer to as "Collectionless AI" pushes towards interactions with the environment, including humans and other artificial agents, to favor dynamic adaptation, customizability, control. At each time instant, data acquired from the environment is only processed with the purpose of contributing to update the current agent-internal representation of the environment, promoting the development of self-organized memorization skills. The goal of this paper is not to introduce new algorithms, but to present an extreme perspective which recovers largely known notions out of the current mainstream, with the goal of stimulating the development of new foundations on computational processes of learning and reasoning. This might open the doors to a truly orthogonal competitive track on AI technologies that avoid data accumulation by design, thus offering a framework which is better suited concerning privacy issues, control and customizability. Pushing towards massively distributed computation, the collectionless approach to AI might reduce the concentration of power in companies and governments, better facing geopolitical issues.

title: Point-KAN: Leveraging Trustworthy AI for Reliable 3-D Point Cloud Completion With Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for 6G-IoT Applications
authors: A. K. Sangaiah; J. Anandakrishnan; S. Kumar; G. -B. Bian; S. A. AlQahtani; D. Draheim
abstract: 3-D point clouds are data points defining the morphology of environments, and completion refers to the reconstruction of missing points. 6G Internet of Things (6G-IoT) connected with 3-D mapping devices needs reliable, consistent, high-fidelity real-time point cloud completion for accurate environment registration. Trustworthy AI, modeled with dependable deep learning (DL), enables reliable and robust point completion with spatial-geometrical consistency for deployment with 6G-IoT devices. Although several DL-based completion techniques are integrated with 6G-IoT devices, they have reliability issues, limiting key trustworthy AI characteristics. This research focuses on the reliability and robustness aspects of trustworthy AI to propose Point-Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN), a dependable real-time 3-D point cloud completion model for 6G IoT-connected 3-D mapping devices. Point-KAN integrates multihead attention and KAN within the modules of attention enhanced-embedded feature collector (AEFC) and KAN-enhanced feature mapper (KEFM) for trustworthy point cloud completion. Empirical evaluations on the ShapeNet demonstrate the superiority of Point-KAN against state-of-the-art (SOTA). Results concrete Point-KAN’s evolution as a trustworthy AI framework ensures reliability and robustness for real-time deployment in 6G-IoT-connected devices, facilitating 3-D environment mapping.

title: Ta Ka Di Mi: AI for Konnakkol and Rhythm Training
authors: S. A. Murthy; B. N. K; V. M. N. Sai
abstract: We present Ta Ka Di Mi, an AI-powered mobile application designed to make rhythm training and Konnakkol-the South Indian art of vocal percussion-accessible to learners worldwide. Konnakkol is a centuries-old tradition where rhythmic syllables are recited to convey complex tala (time cycles or rhythmic frameworks), often serving as both a pedagogical tool and a performance art. While deeply rooted in South Indian classical music, rhythm itself is a universal language, integral to music, dance, speech, and movement across cultures. Despite this universality, learning Konnakkol has traditionally required close mentorship, consistent practice, and significant exposure to expert practitioners, making it less accessible outside specialized communities. Our system addresses these challenges by combining modern AI technologies with carefully curated pedagogical content to create an interactive, scalable, and userfriendly learning experience for global audiences. The application integrates automatic speech recognition, audio signal processing, and real-time feedback models to evaluate learners across multiple dimensions: rhythmic accuracy, pronunciation fidelity, and tempo consistency. Through gamified lessons, learners can progress from foundational exercises to advanced rhythmic improvisations, guided by structured modules designed in collaboration with renowned artist B.C. Manjunath. The AIdriven evaluation engine provides instant personalized feedback, enabling learners to refine their skills iteratively and at their own pace. In addition, the app incorporates adaptive learning strategies that track a user's growth over time and dynamically suggest exercises tailored to individual strengths and weaknesses. Our demo highlights the unique intersection of cultural heritage and modern AI, showcasing how domain-specific AI/ML techniques can be applied to music education in a globally meaningful way. Beyond traditional music training, Ta Ka Di Mi supports diverse use cases, including rhythm practice for dancers and instrumentalists, therapeutic interventions for speech and motor coordination, and cross-cultural exploration for learners worldwide who seek rhythm as a bridge across traditions. By blending ancient tradition with contemporary technology, the platform not only preserves and disseminates an important cultural practice but also reimagines how rhythm can be taught, experienced, and shared universally. Ultimately, Ta Ka Di Mi demonstrates how AI can democratize access to art forms, enhance pedagogy through personalized insights, and foster global community-building around rhythm. In bridging the gap between ancient tradition and modern technology, the system illustrates the potential of AI-powered education platforms to enrich cultural learning and inspire new creative possibilities across the world. title: Classification of Music Genres based on Machine Learning SVM and CNN
authors: A. Pranolo; S. Sularso; N. Anwar; A. B. P. Utama; A. P. Wibawa; R. A. Rachman
abstract: This study aims to compare the performance of two classification methods—Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)—in identifying music genres based on audio data from the GTZAN dataset. Data in a 30-second audio file is converted into a numerical and visual representation (Mel Spectrogram) for each model. The evaluation used precision, recall, and f1-score metrics and was supported by a confusion matrix. Results showed that SVM had higher accuracy (75%) than CNN (71.5%), with more stable performance in most genres. CNN showed superiority in certain genres, such as classical and hip-hop, but experienced a decline in accuracy in genres such as disco and rock. This analysis confirms that the selection of classification models should consider the characteristics of data and genres and open up opportunities for hybrid approaches or the use of more complex architectures in music classification.

title: The Analysis of Multi-Track Music Generation With Deep Learning Models in Music Production Process
authors: R. Jiang; X. Mou
abstract: This study aims to explore the application of deep learning models in multi-track music generation to enhance the efficiency and quality of music production. Considering the limited capability of traditional methods in extracting and representing audio features, a multi-track music generation model based on the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) Transformer network is proposed. This model first utilizes the BERT model to encode and represent music data, capturing semantic and emotional information within the music data. Subsequently, the encoded music features are inputted into the Transformer network to learn the temporal relationships and structural patterns among music sequences, thereby generating new multi-track music compositions. The performance of this model is evaluated, revealing that compared to other algorithms, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 95.98% in music generation prediction, with an improvement in precision by 4.77%. Particularly, the model demonstrates significant advantages in predicting pitch of music tracks. Hence, the multi-track music generation model proposed in this study exhibits excellent performance in accuracy and pitch prediction, offering valuable experimental reference for research and practice in the field of multi-track music generation.

title: CLGA-Net: Holistic Hybrid Deep Learning and Optimization Framework for Advanced Motion Prediction and Analysis in Video Processing
authors: S. Abraham; T. Kanimozhi
abstract: For applications like surveillance, human activity recognition, and autonomous systems, the process of motion prediction from video processing is vital where traditional approaches suffer with factors like computational efficiency, accuracy, adaptability, and so on. Integrating deep learning architectures, a holistic hybrid DL and optimization framework is designed in this paper that is used in enhancing motion prediction. Infused with CNN for spatial features extraction and LSTM module for motion sequence learning, the structured holistic framework ensures accurate motion prediction. The CLGA-Net is further optimized using the hybrid optimization module that consists of Genetic Algorithm and Adaptive Gradient-based Optimization for hyperparameter optimization and fine-tuning weights. Through the validation on metrics like accuracy (90%), robustness, and efficiency of the model on the UCF101 dataset, the findings reveal that the proposed model is well suited for implementations like object tracking, anomaly detection, and gesture recognition.

title: Content Understanding and Reasoning Enhanced Small-Sample Blind Image Quality Assessment
authors: T. Song; D. Cheng; Q. Kou; S. Zhang; Y. Huang; L. Li
abstract: In recent years, small-sample blind image quality assessment (BIQA) has gained considerable attention for its ability to minimize dependence on expensive labeled data. However, as the sample size shrinks, both prediction accuracy and generalization performance decline significantly. A key challenge is that models trained with small datasets struggle to handle diverse image content and lack a clear understanding of how content affects quality. Motivated by the above facts, we propose a content understanding and reasoning enhanced small-sample BIQA framework. In terms of content understanding, we preserve existing understanding capabilities while enhancing adaptability to new scenarios. Specifically, a large multimodal model (LMM) is employed to generate detailed content descriptions, while a distribution-based preservation strategy is further proposed to maintain the image-text similarity understanding capability, thereby mitigating overfitting and catastrophic forgetting. Meanwhile, we propose a contrastive learning framework in which content descriptions are refined by a large language model (LLM) into contrastive ‘real-opposite’ text pairs, enabling the BIQA model to adapt to unseen scenarios by aligning with authentic semantics while distinguishing counterexamples. In terms of content-quality relation learning, we first design quality-guided chain-of-thought strategy to explicitly uncover the relation between content and quality, and distill these reasoning patterns into concise quality-content relations, which then guide the prediction process. Extensive experimental results show that the proposed method not only achieved state-of-art prediction accuracy but also achieved decent generalization ability. The code can be available at https://github.com/esnthere/CURE-IQA.

title: An Extensive Exploration Of Deep Learning Methods for Raga Recognition in Indian Classical Music
authors: A. Jiju; A. V. V
abstract: Indian Classical Music or Shastriya Sangeet, an essential aspect of Indian cultural heritage, is a rich and intricate art form encompassing two major traditions: Hindustani and Carnatic. A fundamental aspect of Indian Classical Music is the raga, which provides the melodic structure for compositions and improvisations. Raga recognition, a vital task in Music Information Retrieval (MIR), facilitates applications such as music recommendation, education, archival, and content-based music retrieval. This paper reviews state-of-the-art methodologies for raga identification, focusing on approaches utilizing deep learning and signal processing techniques. Methods explored include feature extraction and classification models which include Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), spectrograms, scalograms, and temporal sequence modeling via LSTM, BiLSTM, CNN, and RNN techniques. Additionally, this work highlights the importance of open-access datasets for large-scale analysis and the challenges inherent in Indian Art Music research, such as sociocultural context, data annotation, and model generalizability. Future prospects for improving raga identification are explored, emphasizing hybrid models, multi-modal techniques, and real-time applications to blend tradition with technology.

title: Deep Learning for Automatic Detection of Musical Instruments in Audio Signals
authors: A. N. Patil; M. Kudari; A. S. Nandeppanavar; P. N. Thotad
abstract: One essential element of music understanding is the ability to recognize the instruments in an auditory recording. The rapidly evolving field of Automatic Musical Instrument Detection (AMID) provides for the identification of instruments in audio signals without the use for the human intervention, hence meeting this need. In this project, it presents a deep learning-based approach to musical instrument classification that is both accurate and effective. We use a curated dataset with 15 instrument classes and 500 audio samples per class to train and assess five cutting-edge models, including VGG16, DenseNet201, ResNet50V2, MobileNetV2, and XceptionNet, using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Before being entered into the models, the audio recordings undergo preprocessing to create spectrogram pictures, which collect both temporal and spatial information. Multiple dataset splits were used in the experiments to confirm each architecture's resilience. Every model demonstrated its efficacy by achieving classification accuracies above 90%. We also created an end-to-end system that predicts the appropriate instrument class from an input raw audio file.

title: Application of Human Posture Recognition and Classification in Performing Arts Education
authors: J. Shen; L. Chen
abstract: This review explores the integration of human posture recognition and classification technologies in performing arts education, focusing on the advancements in deep learning, neural networks, and computer vision. It traces the evolution of these technologies and highlights their significance in developing personalized teaching methods for performing arts. Following this, we examine various posture recognition technologies, emphasizing data acquisition and processing methods while revealing their strengths and limitations, particularly in their adaptability to performing arts. Moreover, the review discusses posture classification methods, addressing the processing and interpretation of data, and the challenges in achieving classification accuracy and efficiency. Illustrative case studies demonstrate the application of these technologies in enhancing teaching and creativity in performing arts, significantly contributing to the skill development and expressiveness of artists and students. Concluding with a critical assessment of the current feasibility of these technologies in performing arts education, the review suggests potential improvements and future directions. It emphasizes the indispensable role of human posture recognition in advancing performing arts education and underscores the need for continued interdisciplinary research in this evolving field.

title: A Web-Based MIDI Platform for Accessible Music Education: A Case Study of Pachelbel's Canon in D
authors: F. -N. Lin; K. -N. Chang; H. -Y. Chen
abstract: This article presents a web-based platform that leverages MIDI, multimedia, AI, and WebSocket technologies to enrich music education. The platform aims to make music more interactive and accessible for students not majoring in music and more inclusive for reluctant, disadvantaged, or disabled learners. By combining synchronized MIDI with multimedia, our platform offers various interaction modalities, allowing users to engage with music through typing, pressing, playing, touching, and waving, with minimal skills required to produce musical notes, chords, or sequences. A distinctive feature of our platform is the incorporation of Pachelbel's Canon in D into our curriculum to demonstrate the system's capabilities and technology-supported pedagogy. A teaching experiment was conducted in a Taiwanese high school involving four teachers and 31 students. The results showed that 87% of the participants found the platform enjoyable and effective in enhancing their comprehension of musical concepts and boosting their motivation to learn music.

title: LLaQo: Towards a Query-Based Coach in Expressive Music Performance Assessment
authors: H. Zhang; V. K. M. Cheung; H. Nishioka; S. Dixon; S. Furuya
abstract: Research in music understanding has extensively explored composition-level attributes such as key, genre, and instrumentation through advanced representations, leading to cross-modal applications using large language models. However, aspects of musical performance such as stylistic expression and technique remain underexplored, along with the potential of using large language models to enhance educational outcomes with customized feedback. To bridge this gap, we introduce LLaQo, a Large Language Query-based music coach that leverages audio language modeling to provide detailed and formative assessments of music performances. We also introduce instruction-tuned query-response datasets that cover a variety of performance dimensions from pitch accuracy to articulation, as well as contextual performance understanding (such as difficulty and performance techniques). Utilizing AudioMAE encoder and Vicuna-7b LLM backend, our model achieved state-of-the-art (SOTA) results in predicting teachers’ performance ratings, as well as in identifying piece difficulty and playing techniques. Textual responses from LLaQo was moreover rated significantly higher compared to other baseline models in a user study using audio-text matching. Our proposed model can thus provide informative answers to open-ended questions related to musical performance from audio data.

title: Chord Recognition and Lyrics Synchronization System with Physical Visualization for Interactive Music Education
authors: J. A. Ramos
abstract: Musical education faces significant challenges in bridging theoretical instruction with practical application, particularly when students attempt to learn contemporary popular music using traditional notation-based approaches. Current commercial platforms prioritize user engagement but lack comprehensive harmonic analysis integration with physical instrument interaction. This paper presents an integrated chord recognition and lyrics synchronization system that combines automated music analysis with physical visualization for interactive piano education. The proposed system integrates the chord-extractor library utilizing the Chordino algorithm for harmonic analysis, OpenAI’s Whisper model for multilingual lyrics transcription, and GPIO-based LED visualization on embedded hardware. The system operates in two distinct phases: an offline analysis phase where audio content undergoes comprehensive chord recognition and lyrics transcription to generate timestamped musical data, followed by a real-time playback phase where pre-processed information synchronizes with LED visualization during instrumental practice. Experimental validation using five globally popular songs spanning multiple genres and languages demonstrates chord recognition accuracy of $\mathbf{7 8. 4 \%}$ and multilingual lyrics transcription achieving 14.9% average Word Error Rate. The complete implementation is available as open-source software, enabling reproducible research and educational applications that transform how students interact with contemporary musical content.

title: College Vocal Music Teaching System Using Long Short-Term Memory and Feed-Forward Neural Network
authors: Y. Fang
abstract: In modern times, college-level vocal music education has increasingly influenced computational methods to provide objective performance evaluation and personalized teaching guidance. However, existing Deep Fuzzy Music Training (DFMT) approach integrates fuzzy logic with Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to assess vocal performances but struggled with challenges like dependency on fuzzy rules and ineffective in capturing long-term dependencies in musical sequences. To overcome these limitations, Long Short-Term Memory-Feed Forward Neural Network (LSTM-FNN) framework is proposed. Primarily, audio recordings and teacher critiques are collected from CRitique dOCUumentS (CROCUS) dataset. Next, audio signals are preprocessed using noise filtering, normalization and frame segmentation, while critiques are cleaned and tokenized. Then, feature extraction is uses pitch analysis, Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) and Root Mean Square (RMS) energy to capture tonal accuracy, vocal timbre and dynamic strength. Further, stacked LSTM learns temporal dependencies and FNN estimates the performance by generating constant proficiency scores and classifies performance levels. Finally, proposed LSTM-FNN developed an intelligent college vocal music teaching system which automatically evaluate student singing performances and offer actionable teaching feedback. Therefore, proposed LSTMFNN framework achieved greater results in accuracy (98.9%), teaching method efficiency (98.5%), music expression (9.7) and feedback response time (0.9 secs) outperforming existing DFMT method.

title: Fake News Detection Using Deep Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
authors: M. Q. Alnabhan; P. Branco
abstract: Nowadays, we witness rapid technological advancements in online communication platforms, with increasing volumes of people using a vast range of communication solutions. The fast flow of information and the enormous number of users opens the door to the publication of non-truthful news, which has the potential to reach many people. Disseminating this news through low- or no-cost channels resulted in a flood of fake news that is difficult to detect by humans. Social media networks are one of these channels that are used to quickly spread this fake news by manipulating it in ways that influence readers in many aspects. That influence appears in a recent example amid the COVID-19 pandemic and various political events such as the recent US presidential elections. Given how this phenomenon impacts society, it is crucial to understand it well and study mechanisms that allow its timely detection. Deep learning (DL) has proven its potential for multiple complex tasks in the last few years with outstanding results. In particular, multiple specialized solutions have been put forward for natural language processing (NLP) tasks. In this paper, we systematically review existing fake news detection (FND) strategies that use DL techniques. We systematically surveyed the existing research articles by investigating the DL algorithms used in the detection process. Our focus then shifts to the datasets utilized in previous research and the effectiveness of the different DL solutions. Special attention was given to the application of strategies for transfer learning and dealing with the class imbalance problem. The effect of these solutions on the detection accuracy is also discussed. Finally, our survey provides an overview of key challenges that remain unsolved in the context of FND.

While ChatGPT enhances efficiency and academic communication, students recognize its limitations and the risks of over-reliance, such as diminished critical thinking and skill development, and increased procrastination. title: A Continuous Hidden Markov Algorithm-Based Multimedia Melody Retrieval System for Music Education
authors: Y. Cheng
abstract: Education professionals receive instruction in Music Education (ME) to prepare for prospective jobs like secondary or primary music teachers, schools ensembles executives, or ensembles directors at music institutions. In the discipline of music education, educators do original research on different approaches to teaching and studying music. The most accurate and effective method of extracting music from huge music databases has become one of the most frequently discussed participants in contemporary multimedia information retrieval development. The essence of multimedia material is presented within a range of techniques since it is not bound to a single side. These several categories could consist of the song's audio components and lyrics for musical information. Retrieving melodic information, subsequently, becomes the main focus of most recent studies. Aside from being an expensive deviate from academics, music programs are neither a viable profession neither a valid pastime. Therefore, in this study, we offer a Continuous Hidden Markov Algorithm (CHMA) related a novel method for recovering melodies from musical multimedia recordings. CHMA is considered to be the most basic dynamic Bayesian network. Two various types of audio frame features and audio example features are extracted throughout the feature extraction procedure from the audio signal according to unit length. Every music clip receives a unique approach that we implement with concurrently using various CHMA. The initial music gets processed using a trained CHMA that monitors fundamental frequencies, maps states, and generates retrieval outcomes. The training time for Traditional opera reached 455.76 minutes, the testing time for Narration achieved 56.10 minutes, and the recognition accuracy for advertisement reached an impressive 98.02%. A subsequently experimental result validates the applicability of the proposed approach.

title: A Kolmogorov Arnold Network NAS Framework for Strumming Pattern Recognition in Technology-Enhanced Pop/Rock Music Education
authors: M. Pennese; S. Giacomelli; C. Rinaldi
abstract: This paper contributes to the Internet of Sounds by presenting a modular neural architecture for automatic classification of guitar strumming patterns in pop/rock music, developed within the Strummin’ Gym project, an interactive platform for technology-enhanced music education. Motivated by the observation that a small set of rhythmic templates recurs across the genre, we frame a novel multinomial classification task to support strumming analysis and instrument learning. We construct and release a curated dataset of annotated audio excerpts from YouTube and extract diverse rhythmic descriptors using LibROSA, Essentia, and the TU-Wien Rhythmic Pattern Extractor. The proposed Neural Networks model combines 1D/2D convolutional-attentive encoders with Kolmogorov–Arnold Net-works, optimized via Neural Architecture Search and Hyper-parameter Tuning. Results show that KANs effectively capture structured audio regularities and confirm the emergence of recurring strumming practices. This work exemplifies how machine listening can enhance IoS applications for inclusive and scalable music education.

title: Automatic Image Evaluation of Doodling Game Using CNN Model
authors: A. M. Amir; A. Primanita; O. Arsalan; D. P. Rini
abstract: In the era of artificial intelligence (AI) development, the integration of machine learning technology in games continues to advance. This study aims to develop a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model that functions as an automatic evaluation agent for doodle images in a drawing game. The CNN model is trained using the Google Quick, Draw! dataset to recognize images created by players. Evaluation of the model is done calculating the accuracy, precision, recall, and $\mathbf{F 1}$-score of each object labels. Labels with recall values less than 0.5 is dropped from the game. Results show that the developed CNN model with 331 labels achieves an accuracy of 0.83. Additionally, other evaluation metrics indicate precision values between 0.6 to 0.96, recall between 0.51 and 0.98, and an F1-score between 0.56 and 0.96. The model’s average prediction time is recorded at 0.002836 seconds, allowing for instant evaluation. The developed CNN model effectively provides feedback to players as long as the input images do not differ significantly from the shapes in the dataset.

title: Stored-Reference LMS Filtering on FPGA for Low- Latency Acoustic Feedback Cancellation in Live Audio Systems
authors: W.S.C.Rodrigo; R. A. P. Buddhika; W.C.Nirmal; A.C.Ranasinghe; S.L.Mallawathanthri
abstract: Acoustic feedback, often perceived as howling, remains a major challenge in live audio environments. This paper presents a real-time feedback suppression system based on a Stored-Reference LMS filtering strategy implemented on an FPGA. The proposed design captures a reference feedback signal during a short detection phase and reuses it during operation for adaptive cancellation. The system was developed on a Zynq-7010 platform with a WM8960 codec and evaluated using both simulation and hardware tests. Objective measurements across multiple audio samples, including music with high-frequency noise and guitar signals containing 600–900 Hz howling show consistent SNR improvement compared to unfiltered audio and a conventional notch-filter baseline. Among the evaluated algorithms, LMS offered the best balance of stability and computational efficiency for FPGA deployment. Results confirm that the stored-reference LMS approach effectively suppresses feedback while preserving audio quality. Future extensions include multi-channel support and dynamic reference adaptation for more complex acoustic environments.

authors: K. -Y. Chen; K. -L. Chen; Y. -C. Yu; J. -J. Ding
abstract: In Music Information Retrieval (MIR), modeling and transforming the tone of musical instruments, particularly electric guitars, has gained increasing attention due to the richness of the instrument tone and the flexibility of expression. Tone morphing enables smooth transitions between different guitar sounds, giving musicians greater freedom to explore new textures and personalize their performances. This study explores learningbased approaches for guitar tone morphing, beginning with LoRA fine-tuning to improve the model performance on limited data. Moreover, we introduce a simpler method, named spherical interpolation using Music2Latent. It yields significantly better results than the more complex fine-tuning approach. title: Enhancing the Teaching of Data Structures and Algorithms using AI Chatbots
authors: M. Y. Hean Low; C. Ching Lee; K. K. Lee; K. Leong Lam
abstract: This paper explores the potential of AI chatbots in enhancing the teaching of data structures and algorithms (DSA) in computer science education. We present our experience using AI chatbots to create multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and investigate students’ feedback in using AI chatbots in their team project assignment. Our findings suggest that while AI chatbots can provide valuable assistance in DSA learning, certain limitations exist. The results of evaluating the AI chatbots on a prompt to generate an MCQ question on the recursive Fibonacci algorithm show that the chatbots did not always provide the correct answers. For the team project assignment, students found AI chatbots to be useful in their learning experience, with high ratings for the accuracy, completeness, clarity, and relevance of the chatbot responses. The students’ feedback also suggests that the chatbots provided a fun and engaging learning experience and that they would like to see more interactive and immersive learning experiences in the future. These results suggest that AI chatbots have great potential to enhance the teaching of DSA by offering personalized and accessible support to students. With ongoing development and refinement, AI chatbots can become invaluable tools for computer science educators and learners alike.

title: Spring Reverb Emulation with Hybrid Gated Convolutional Networks and State Space Models
authors: J. Janser; M. Wess; D. Dallinger; M. Bittner; D. Schnöll; A. Jantsch
abstract: Modeling analog audio effects like spring reverbs is a long-standing challenge due to their complex, nonlinear behaviors, such as amplitude-dependent transients and long, dispersive reverberant tails. While deep learning has shown promising results, existing approaches often struggle to capture these characteristics simultaneously. In this paper, we propose GCN-SSM, a novel hybrid model architecture that combines a Gated Convolutional Network (GCN) with a State Space Model (SSM), leveraging sequential blocks of interleaved feedforward and recurrent layers. We evaluate the performance with spectral and time-domain losses, and a MUSHRA listening test. Our results show that both components are critical for achieving state-of-the-art perceptual quality. The GCN-SSM consistently outperforms the non-hybrid GCN across all metrics. With only 125.7k parameters and inference requiring 5.9 GFLOP for 1 second of audio at 44.1 kHz, the GCN-SSM is theoretically suitable for deployment on modern CPUs.
